Ingested Gemini Notes appear here once matched to this student.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t77 heading POSTED TO THEIR CLASSROOM, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t78 text POSTED TO THEIR CLASSROOM\n\t\t\t\t\t\t93 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t94 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t95 text Some, Most, and All Session recap  ·  Sep 29, 2026\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t96 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t97 text Quantity statements tell us whether a claim applies to some members of a group, most of them, or all of them. Suppose a class has been assigned a case to read. “Some students read it,” “most students read it,” and “all students read it” are three different claims about that same class. We do not need an exact headcount to understand the difference. For each sentence, ask: \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t98 text What must be true? What could still be true?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t99 text  The answer changes with the word we use.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t100 heading Some guarantees at least one, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t101 text Some guarantees at least one\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t102 text Imagine a shelf with eight books. I tell you that \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t103 text some of the books are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t104 text . How many hardcover books must there be? At least \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t105 text one\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t106 text . There could be one, four, or all eight. “Some” rules out zero. It does not rule out “most” or “all.” This is easy to miss because in ordinary conversation “some” often suggests “some, but not all.” On the LSAT, that extra phrase is not part of the statement. If all eight books are hardcover, it is still true that some are hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t107 text Try it:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t108 text  “Some applicants received an interview.” Could every applicant have received one? Does the sentence tell us that anyone was denied an interview?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t109 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t110 text Every applicant could have received an interview. The sentence does not tell us that anyone was denied one. “Some” guarantees at least one applicant received an interview, but it leaves open how many others did. Whenever you read \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t111 text some\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t112 text , replace it with \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t113 text at least one\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t114 text  in your head. That tells you exactly what the sentence guarantees:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t115 text Some of the books are hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t116 text At least one of the books is hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t117 text Now focus on that one book. It belongs to both groups: it is a book, and it is hardcover. If we describe the same object from the hardcover side, we can say:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t118 text Some hardcover items are books.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t119 text At least one hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t120 text We have not found a new object. We have described the same overlap in the other direction. That is why a \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t121 text some\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t122 text  statement works both ways:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t123 text Books  ←some→  Hardcover\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t124 text The double arrow tells us that at least one thing belongs to both groups. It does not tell us that every book is hardcover or that every hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t125 heading What would make “some” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t126 text What would make “some” false?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t127 text If \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t128 text some books are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t129 text  is false, then \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t130 text no books are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t131 text . There is not even one book in both groups. Notice the difference between \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t132 text no books are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t133 text  and \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t134 text some books are not hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t135 text . The second sentence still allows other books to be hardcover, so it does not negate “some.”\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t136 heading Most guarantees more than half, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t137 text Most guarantees more than half\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t138 text Now I tell you that \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t139 text most of the eight books are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t140 text . We need at least \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t141 text five\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t142 text  hardcover books. Four would be exactly half, and half is not most. Five, six, seven, or eight could satisfy the sentence. Notice that all eight could still be hardcover. “Most” does not tell us that an exception exists.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t143 text Try it:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t144 text  If most of the eight books are hardcover, must some of them be hardcover? Must any be paperback?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t145 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t146 text At least five are hardcover, so \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t147 text some are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t148 text . No paperback book is required. All eight could be hardcover. Here is where the direction of the statement matters. From “most books are hardcover,” we know that \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t149 text some hardcover things are books\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t150 text . We cannot say that \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t151 text most hardcover things are books\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t152 text . Five of our eight shelf books could be hardcover, while a library holds hundreds of other hardcover items. The first statement counts the eight books; the reversed statement counts a different group.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t153 text Books  ─most→  Hardcover\nHardcover  ←some→  Books\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t154 text The first arrow gives the majority claim. The second line is the overlap that the majority guarantees. When we read a most statement backward, the word becomes \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t155 text some\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t156 text .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t157 text Quick check:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t158 text  A program has 100 applicants. Most speak Spanish. What is the smallest possible number who speak Spanish? What is the largest?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t159 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t160 text 51 to 100.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t161 text  Fifty is only half. “Most” also permits all 100, so it does not establish an exception.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t162 heading What would make “most” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t163 text What would make “most” false?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t164 text “Most of the eight books are hardcover” needs at least five hardcover books. Its negation permits \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t165 text four or fewer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t166 text . Four is exactly half, so it already makes “most” false. The opposite of “most are hardcover” is \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t167 text half or fewer are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t168 text , not “most are paperback.” Both kinds could make up exactly half.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t169 heading All leaves no exception, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t170 text All leaves no exception\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t171 text If \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t172 text all eight books are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t173 text , every book on the shelf is hardcover. One paperback on that shelf would make the statement false. An all statement gives us a rule: \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t174 text if it is one of these eight books, then it is hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t175 text .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t176 text One of these books  →  Hardcover\nNot hardcover       →  Not one of these books\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t177 text The second line is the contrapositive. Both lines go with the same rule. We cannot turn the first line around and conclude that every hardcover thing is a book on this shelf.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t178 text Try it:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t179 text  You pick up a paperback. What does the rule tell you? What if you pick up a hardcover book from another shelf?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t180 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t181 text The paperback cannot be one of these eight books. A hardcover book from another shelf does not become one of these eight just because it is hardcover. Being hardcover is required, but it is not enough to identify one of these books. There is a small qualification. “All A are B” gives a rule about A. By itself, it does not tell us that any A exist. When we already know the group exists, all also guarantees most and some.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t182 heading What would make “all” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t183 text What would make “all” false?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t184 text One exception is enough. “Not all eight books are hardcover” means \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t185 text at least one of the eight is not hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t186 text . The other seven could still be hardcover. This is the negation of the all claim. By contrast, “not hardcover → not one of these eight books” is its \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t187 text contrapositive\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t188 text : another way to state the original rule, not a way to deny it.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t189 heading Put the three statements side by side, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t190 text Put the three statements side by side\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t191 text The same shelf can help us see the whole range. Read the implications in one direction:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t192 text ALL  →  MOST  →  SOME       (when the group exists)\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t193 text If all eight books are hardcover, then most are, and some are. If only “some” is given, all eight \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t194 text could\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t195 text  be hardcover, but we cannot conclude that they \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t196 text are\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t197 text . Keep the distinction between a possible situation and a required one.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t198 heading Carry a claim through an all rule, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t199 text Carry a claim through an all rule\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t200 text Now we can combine statements. Suppose \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t201 text some library books are mysteries\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t202 text  and \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t203 text all mysteries are fiction\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t204 text . We have at least one book that is a mystery. The all rule applies to every mystery, including that one. So \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t205 text some library books are fiction\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t206 text .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t207 text Library books  ←some→  Mysteries  →  Fiction\nLibrary books  ←some→  Fiction\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t208 text The all arrow points \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t209 text away from\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t210 text  the mystery group we reached. That is why the chain works. If the second sentence said only “most mysteries are fiction,” the mystery books we found could be among the exceptions.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t211 text Quick check:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t212 text  Some archive documents are letters. All letters are handwritten. What follows?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t213 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t214 text Some archive documents are handwritten.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t215 text  Take a document guaranteed to be a letter. The all rule applies to that document. The same reasoning preserves the first quantity word: | First statement | Rule | What follows | |---|---|---| | Some library books are mysteries. | All mysteries are fiction. | Some library books are fiction. | | Most library books are mysteries. | All mysteries are fiction. | Most library books are fiction. | | All library books are mysteries. | All mysteries are fiction. | All library books are fiction. |\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t216 text Try it:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t217 text  “Most library books are mysteries. All fiction is mystery.” Can we conclude that most library books are fiction?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t218 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t219 text No. The all arrow goes from fiction to mystery. We cannot start at mystery and travel backward to fiction.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t220 heading Two majorities of the same group must meet, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t221 text Two majorities of the same group must meet\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t222 text Suppose a club has ten members. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t223 text Most members study law\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t224 text , and \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t225 text most members work part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t226 text . Each “most” needs at least six of the ten members. Those two sets cannot fit inside the club without sharing at least two people.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t227 text What is given?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t228 text  More than half of the \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t229 text same ten members\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t230 text  study law. More than half of those same ten work part time. The claims count club members, not all law students or all part-time workers everywhere.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t231 text Why must they meet?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t232 text  Each group needs at least six members. If the groups were separate, we would need twelve different club members. There are only ten. At least two members must be in both groups.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t233 text What follows?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t234 text Some law students work part time.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t235 text  We can reverse that some claim: \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t236 text some part-time workers study law\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t237 text . Both sentences describe the same overlapping members. We know at least one exists; we do not know that most law students or most part-time workers have the other trait.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t238 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             Most club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         Both majorities count the same club members.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t239 text Quick check:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t240 text  A club has 25 members. Most are lawyers, and most play an instrument. What is the smallest possible number who are both lawyers and play an instrument?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t241 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t242 text One.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t243 text  Each majority needs at least 13 members. If none overlapped, those groups would require 26 different people, but the club has only 25. All 25 could also have both traits.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t244 text Try it:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t245 text  If most club members study law and most club members work part time, could the two groups of members be completely separate?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t246 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t247 text No. Two separate majorities would require more members than the club has. At least one member must have both traits.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t248 heading When all describes that same group, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t249 text When all describes that same group\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t250 text There is another way to guarantee an overlap. Suppose \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t251 text most club members study law\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t252 text , and \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t253 text all club members work part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t254 text . We already know there are law students in the club. The all rule tells us that \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t255 text each one of those members\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t256 text  also works part time. So \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t257 text some law students work part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t258 text .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t259 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             All club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         The law students already found are club members,\n             so the all rule applies to each of them.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t260 text We can make the same move with \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t261 text some\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t262 text . If \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t263 text some club members study law\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t264 text  and \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t265 text all club members work part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t266 text , take the member guaranteed by “some.” That person has both traits. Again, \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t267 text some law students work part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t268 text . The sentences can be stated in the other order: \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t269 text all club members work part time; some club members study law\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t270 text . The same person still proves the overlap.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t271 text Try it:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t272 text  All A are B. All A are C. Must some B be C?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t273 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t274 text Not yet. The two all rules tell us what is true \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t275 text if\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t276 text  something is A, but neither tells us that any A exists. Add “at least one A exists,” and the overlap follows.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t277 heading Two majorities can also compare group sizes, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t278 text Two majorities can also compare group sizes\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t279 text Here is a different comparison. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t280 text Most debate team members are seniors\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t281 text , but \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t282 text most seniors are not on the debate team\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t283 text . The seniors on the team are more than half of the team and less than half of the seniors. The same overlap takes up a larger share of the team than of the senior class. Therefore, \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t284 text there are more seniors than debate team members\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t285 text . The numbers in the picture are one possible case. The conclusion follows from the two majority claims, not from those particular numbers.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t286 heading Similar chains can leave a gap, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t287 text Similar chains can leave a gap\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t288 text Two some statements need not describe the same person or thing:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t289 text Some volunteers speak Spanish.\nSome Spanish speakers are trained.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t290 text The trained Spanish speakers could all be people who do not volunteer. We cannot conclude that any volunteers are trained. Replacing the second “some” with “most” does not fix the gap. The Spanish-speaking volunteers could sit in the untrained minority. Even two most statements that count different groups do not automatically produce a new majority claim. Before drawing a conclusion, ask: \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t291 text Am I carrying a known group through an all rule? Or do two majorities count the same group?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t292 text  If neither is true, check whether the groups could miss each other.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t293 text Quick check:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t294 text  A club has 13 members. Most are women, and some are dancers. How many female dancers are guaranteed? How many are possible?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t295 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t296 text Zero are guaranteed; as many as 13 are possible.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t297 text  Seven women and one dancer meet the statements even if that dancer is one of the six men. Both traits could also belong to every member. A most claim and a some claim about the same group do not force the two traits to meet.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t298 heading The moves to keep, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t299 text The moves to keep\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t300 text | What you have | What you may conclude | |---|---| | Some A are B | Some B are A | | Most A are B | Some A are B, and some B are A | | All A are B | A → B, and not B → not A | | Some/most/all A are B; all B are C | The same first quantity of A are C | | Most A are B; most A are C | Some B are C | | Most A are B; all A are C | Some B are C | | Some A are B; all A are C | Some B are C | Two \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t301 text all\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t302 text  claims about A guarantee that every A has both traits. They guarantee \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t303 text some B are C\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t304 text  only when we also know that at least one A exists. Use the sentence behind each arrow to check what it guarantees.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t305 heading Nearby words need a closer look, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t306 text Nearby words need a closer look\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t307 text The words around a quantity statement can look familiar without making the same promise. Sort them by \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t308 text what they guarantee\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t309 text , then check the sentence in front of you: | Word or phrase | What it guarantees | |---|---| | \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t310 text Some\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t311 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t312 text at least one\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t313 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t314 text one or more\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t315 text  | One or more members fit. All may fit too. | | \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t316 text A few\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t317 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t318 text several\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t319 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t320 text many\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t321 text  | A positive number in ordinary use, but no universal cutoff. They imply at least one. | | \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t322 text Most\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t323 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t324 text more than half\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t325 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t326 text a majority of\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t327 text  | Strictly more than half of the named group fit. | | \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t328 text All\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t329 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t330 text every\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t331 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t332 text each\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t333 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t334 text without exception\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t335 text  | Every member of the named group fits. The group may still need a separate existence premise. | | \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t336 text Few\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t337 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t338 text not many\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t339 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t340 text not often\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t341 text  | A small number or low frequency in context. No exact numerical boundary follows. | | \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t342 text No\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t343 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t344 text none\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t345 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t346 text zero\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t347 text  | Not a single member fits. | | \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t348 text Not all\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t349 text  | At least one member does \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t350 text not\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t351 text  fit. |\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t352 text Few\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t353 text  is worth separating from \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t354 text a few\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t355 text . “A few books are hardcover” affirms that at least some are. “Few books are hardcover” stresses how small the number is. It often suggests some in ordinary speech, but it does not set a dependable numerical minimum. “Not many” can include zero. A hundred menu items could make five feel like few; in a menu of six, five would not feel like few. Do not quietly replace any of these phrases with a fixed number.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t356 text Most\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t357 text  is different: it crosses a precise line, \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t358 text more than half\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t359 text . Words such as \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t360 text the majority\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t361 text  plainly express that idea. Words such as \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t362 text usually\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t363 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t364 text typically\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t365 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t366 text generally\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t367 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t368 text commonly\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t369 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t370 text frequently\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t371 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t372 text often\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t373 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t374 text likely\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t375 text , and \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t376 text probably\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t377 text  can suggest prevalence in context, but pay attention to what the sentence actually counts. “Probably” about one event, for example, is a likelihood claim, not a headcount of a group.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t378 text Not all\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t379 text does\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t380 text  give us a precise minimum: at least one exception. “Not all club members are lawyers” means \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t381 text at least one club member is not a lawyer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t382 text . It does not tell us whether the other members are lawyers.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t383 text Quick check:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t384 text  A menu lists 100 beers. “Many are Belgian,” “few are Belgian,” and “not many are Belgian” are three claims. Can you assign each one an exact minimum and maximum? What does “not all are Belgian” guarantee?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t385 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t386 text The first three do \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t387 text not\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t388 text  have fixed numerical boundaries. “Many” suggests more than an isolated example, while “few” and “not many” suggest a small number relative to the context. None alone licenses a specific cutoff such as five or ten. “Not all” is exact about one thing: \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t389 text at least one beer is not Belgian\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t390 text .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t391 heading Pop quiz: decide whether the overlap follows, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t392 text Pop quiz: decide whether the overlap follows\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t393 text For each pair, decide whether it guarantees \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t394 text some A are C\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t395 text . Draw a witness or explain where the groups could miss each other before reading the answers.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t396 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t397 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t398 AXListMarker 1. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t399 text Some A are B. All B are C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t400 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t401 AXListMarker 2. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t402 text Some A are B. Most A are C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t403 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t404 AXListMarker 3. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t405 text All A are B. Some B are C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t406 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t407 AXListMarker 4. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t408 text Some A are B. Most B are C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t409 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t410 AXListMarker 5. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t411 text Some A are B. Some B are C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t412 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t413 AXListMarker 6. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t414 text Most A are B. Most A are C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t415 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t416 AXListMarker 7. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t417 text All A are B. All A are C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t418 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t419 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t420 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t421 AXListMarker 1. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t422 text Yes.  The A that is B must also be C because every B is C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t423 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t424 AXListMarker 2. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t425 text No.  The A that is B could be outside the majority of A that is C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t426 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t427 AXListMarker 3. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t428 text No.  The B that is C could be outside A. The all rule runs from A to B, not back from B to A.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t429 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t430 AXListMarker 4. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t431 text No.  The known A that is B could be among the B that are not C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t432 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t433 AXListMarker 5. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t434 text No.  The B in the first statement could differ from the B in the second.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t435 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t436 AXListMarker 6. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t437 text Yes.  Two majorities of the same A group must share at least one member, who is both B and C.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t438 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t439 AXListMarker 7. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t440 text Not from these statements alone.  Every A would be both B and C, but the statements do not establish that an A exists. Ingested Gemini Notes appear here once matched to this student.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t77 heading POSTED TO THEIR CLASSROOM, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t78 text POSTED TO THEIR CLASSROOM\n\t\t\t\t\t\t93 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t94 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t95 text Some, Most, and All Session recap  ·  Sep 29, 2026\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t506 text Quantity statements tell us whether a claim applies to some members of a group, most of them, or all of them. Suppose a class has been assigned a case to read. “Some students read it,” “most students read it,” and “all students read it” are three different claims about that same class. We do not need an exact headcount to understand the difference.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t507 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t508 text For each sentence, ask:  What must be true? What could still be true?  The answer changes with the word we use.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t509 heading Some guarantees at least one, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t510 text Some guarantees at least one\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t511 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t512 text Imagine a shelf with eight books. I tell you that  some of the books are hardcover . How many hardcover books must there be?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t513 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t514 text At least  one . There could be one, four, or all eight. “Some” rules out zero. It does not rule out “most” or “all.”\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t515 text This is easy to miss because in ordinary conversation “some” often suggests “some, but not all.” On the LSAT, that extra phrase is not part of the statement. If all eight books are hardcover, it is still true that some are hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t516 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t517 text Try it:  “Some applicants received an interview.” Could every applicant have received one? Does the sentence tell us that anyone was denied an interview?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t518 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t519 text Every applicant could have received an interview. The sentence does not tell us that anyone was denied one. “Some” guarantees at least one applicant received an interview, but it leaves open how many others did.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t520 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t521 text Whenever you read  some , replace it with  at least one  in your head. That tells you exactly what the sentence guarantees:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t522 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t523 text Some of the books are hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t524 text At least one of the books is hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t525 text Now focus on that one book. It belongs to both groups: it is a book, and it is hardcover. If we describe the same object from the hardcover side, we can say:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t526 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t527 text Some hardcover items are books.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t528 text At least one hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t529 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t530 text We have not found a new object. We have described the same overlap in the other direction. That is why a  some  statement works both ways:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t531 text Books  ←some→  Hardcover\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t532 text The double arrow tells us that at least one thing belongs to both groups. It does not tell us that every book is hardcover or that every hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t533 heading What would make “some” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t534 text What would make “some” false?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t535 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t536 text If  some books are hardcover  is false, then  no books are hardcover . There is not even one book in both groups. Notice the difference between  no books are hardcover  and  some books are not hardcover . The second sentence still allows other books to be hardcover, so it does not negate “some.”\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t537 heading Most guarantees more than half, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t538 text Most guarantees more than half\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t539 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t540 text Now I tell you that  most of the eight books are hardcover . We need at least  five  hardcover books. Four would be exactly half, and half is not most. Five, six, seven, or eight could satisfy the sentence.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t541 text Notice that all eight could still be hardcover. “Most” does not tell us that an exception exists.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t542 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t543 text Try it:  If most of the eight books are hardcover, must some of them be hardcover? Must any be paperback?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t544 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t545 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t546 text At least five are hardcover, so  some are hardcover . No paperback book is required. All eight could be hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t547 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t548 text Here is where the direction of the statement matters. From “most books are hardcover,” we know that  some hardcover things are books . We cannot say that  most hardcover things are books . Five of our eight shelf books could be hardcover, while a library holds hundreds of other hardcover items. The first statement counts the eight books; the reversed statement counts a different group.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t549 text Books  ─most→  Hardcover\nHardcover  ←some→  Books\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t550 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t551 text The first arrow gives the majority claim. The second line is the overlap that the majority guarantees. When we read a most statement backward, the word becomes  some .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t552 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t553 text Quick check:  A program has 100 applicants. Most speak Spanish. What is the smallest possible number who speak Spanish? What is the largest?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t554 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t555 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t556 text 51 to 100.  Fifty is only half. “Most” also permits all 100, so it does not establish an exception.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t557 heading What would make “most” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t558 text What would make “most” false?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t559 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t560 text “Most of the eight books are hardcover” needs at least five hardcover books. Its negation permits  four or fewer . Four is exactly half, so it already makes “most” false. The opposite of “most are hardcover” is  half or fewer are hardcover , not “most are paperback.” Both kinds could make up exactly half.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t561 heading All leaves no exception, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t562 text All leaves no exception\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t563 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t564 text If  all eight books are hardcover , every book on the shelf is hardcover. One paperback on that shelf would make the statement false.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t565 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t566 text An all statement gives us a rule:  if it is one of these eight books, then it is hardcover .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t567 text One of these books  →  Hardcover\nNot hardcover       →  Not one of these books\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t568 text The second line is the contrapositive. Both lines go with the same rule. We cannot turn the first line around and conclude that every hardcover thing is a book on this shelf.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t569 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t570 text Try it:  You pick up a paperback. What does the rule tell you? What if you pick up a hardcover book from another shelf?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t571 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t572 text The paperback cannot be one of these eight books. A hardcover book from another shelf does not become one of these eight just because it is hardcover. Being hardcover is required, but it is not enough to identify one of these books.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t573 text There is a small qualification. “All A are B” gives a rule about A. By itself, it does not tell us that any A exist. When we already know the group exists, all also guarantees most and some.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t574 heading What would make “all” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t575 text What would make “all” false?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t576 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t577 text One exception is enough. “Not all eight books are hardcover” means  at least one of the eight is not hardcover . The other seven could still be hardcover. This is the negation of the all claim. By contrast, “not hardcover → not one of these eight books” is its  contrapositive : another way to state the original rule, not a way to deny it.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t578 heading Put the three statements side by side, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t579 text Put the three statements side by side\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t580 text The same shelf can help us see the whole range.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t581 text Read the implications in one direction:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t582 text ALL  →  MOST  →  SOME       (when the group exists)\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t583 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t584 text If all eight books are hardcover, then most are, and some are. If only “some” is given, all eight  could  be hardcover, but we cannot conclude that they  are . Keep the distinction between a possible situation and a required one.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t585 heading Carry a claim through an all rule, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t586 text Carry a claim through an all rule\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t587 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t588 text Now we can combine statements. Suppose  some library books are mysteries  and  all mysteries are fiction . We have at least one book that is a mystery. The all rule applies to every mystery, including that one. So  some library books are fiction .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t589 text Library books  ←some→  Mysteries  →  Fiction\nLibrary books  ←some→  Fiction\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t590 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t591 text The all arrow points  away from  the mystery group we reached. That is why the chain works. If the second sentence said only “most mysteries are fiction,” the mystery books we found could be among the exceptions.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t592 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t593 text Quick check:  Some archive documents are letters. All letters are handwritten. What follows?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t594 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t595 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t596 text Some archive documents are handwritten.  Take a document guaranteed to be a letter. The all rule applies to that document.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t597 text The same reasoning preserves the first quantity word:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t598 text | First statement | Rule | What follows | |---|---|---| | Some library books are mysteries. | All mysteries are fiction. | Some library books are fiction. | | Most library books are mysteries. | All mysteries are fiction. | Most library books are fiction. | | All library books are mysteries. | All mysteries are fiction. | All library books are fiction. |\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t599 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t600 text Try it:  “Most library books are mysteries. All fiction is mystery.” Can we conclude that most library books are fiction?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t601 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t602 text No. The all arrow goes from fiction to mystery. We cannot start at mystery and travel backward to fiction.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t603 heading Two majorities of the same group must meet, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t604 text Two majorities of the same group must meet\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t605 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t606 text Suppose a club has ten members.  Most members study law , and  most members work part time . Each “most” needs at least six of the ten members. Those two sets cannot fit inside the club without sharing at least two people.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t607 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t608 text What is given?  More than half of the  same ten members  study law. More than half of those same ten work part time. The claims count club members, not all law students or all part-time workers everywhere.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t609 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t610 text Why must they meet?  Each group needs at least six members. If the groups were separate, we would need twelve different club members. There are only ten. At least two members must be in both groups.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t611 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t612 text What follows? Some law students work part time.  We can reverse that some claim:  some part-time workers study law . Both sentences describe the same overlapping members. We know at least one exists; we do not know that most law students or most part-time workers have the other trait.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t613 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             Most club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         Both majorities count the same club members.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t614 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t615 text Quick check:  A club has 25 members. Most are lawyers, and most play an instrument. What is the smallest possible number who are both lawyers and play an instrument?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t616 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t617 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t618 text One.  Each majority needs at least 13 members. If none overlapped, those groups would require 26 different people, but the club has only 25. All 25 could also have both traits.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t619 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t620 text Try it:  If most club members study law and most club members work part time, could the two groups of members be completely separate?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t621 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t622 text No. Two separate majorities would require more members than the club has. At least one member must have both traits.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t623 heading When all describes that same group, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t624 text When all describes that same group\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t625 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t626 text There is another way to guarantee an overlap. Suppose  most club members study law , and  all club members work part time . We already know there are law students in the club. The all rule tells us that  each one of those members  also works part time. So  some law students work part time .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t627 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             All club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         The law students already found are club members,\n             so the all rule applies to each of them.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t628 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t629 text We can make the same move with  some . If  some club members study law  and  all club members work part time , take the member guaranteed by “some.” That person has both traits. Again,  some law students work part time . The sentences can be stated in the other order:  all club members work part time; some club members study law . The same person still proves the overlap.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t630 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t631 text Try it:  All A are B. All A are C. Must some B be C?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t632 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t633 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t634 text Not yet. The two all rules tell us what is true  if  something is A, but neither tells us that any A exists. Add “at least one A exists,” and the overlap follows.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t635 heading Two majorities can also compare group sizes, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t636 text Two majorities can also compare group sizes\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t637 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t638 text Here is a different comparison.  Most debate team members are seniors , but  most seniors are not on the debate team . The seniors on the team are more than half of the team and less than half of the seniors. The same overlap takes up a larger share of the team than of the senior class. Therefore,  there are more seniors than debate team members .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t639 text The numbers in the picture are one possible case. The conclusion follows from the two majority claims, not from those particular numbers.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t640 heading Similar chains can leave a gap, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t641 text Similar chains can leave a gap\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t642 text Two some statements need not describe the same person or thing:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t643 text Some volunteers speak Spanish.\nSome Spanish speakers are trained.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t644 text The trained Spanish speakers could all be people who do not volunteer. We cannot conclude that any volunteers are trained.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t645 text Replacing the second “some” with “most” does not fix the gap. The Spanish-speaking volunteers could sit in the untrained minority. Even two most statements that count different groups do not automatically produce a new majority claim.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t646 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t647 text Before drawing a conclusion, ask:  Am I carrying a known group through an all rule? Or do two majorities count the same group?  If neither is true, check whether the groups could miss each other.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t648 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t649 text Quick check:  A club has 13 members. Most are women, and some are dancers. How many female dancers are guaranteed? How many are possible?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t650 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t651 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t652 text Zero are guaranteed; as many as 13 are possible.  Seven women and one dancer meet the statements even if that dancer is one of the six men. Both traits could also belong to every member. A most claim and a some claim about the same group do not force the two traits to meet.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t653 heading The moves to keep, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t654 text The moves to keep\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t655 text | What you have | What you may conclude | |---|---| | Some A are B | Some B are A | | Most A are B | Some A are B, and some B are A | | All A are B | A → B, and not B → not A | | Some/most/all A are B; all B are C | The same first quantity of A are C | | Most A are B; most A are C | Some B are C | | Most A are B; all A are C | Some B are C | | Some A are B; all A are C | Some B are C |\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t656 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t657 text Two  all  claims about A guarantee that every A has both traits. They guarantee  some B are C  only when we also know that at least one A exists.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t658 text Use the sentence behind each arrow to check what it guarantees.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t659 heading Nearby words need a closer look, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t660 text Nearby words need a closer look\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t661 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t662 text The words around a quantity statement can look familiar without making the same promise. Sort them by  what they guarantee , then check the sentence in front of you:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t663 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t664 text | Word or phrase | What it guarantees | |---|---| |  Some ,  at least one ,  one or more  | One or more members fit. All may fit too. | |  A few ,  several ,  many  | A positive number in ordinary use, but no universal cutoff. They imply at least one. | |  Most ,  more than half ,  a majority of  | Strictly more than half of the named group fit. | |  All ,  every ,  each ,  without exception  | Every member of the named group fits. The group may still need a separate existence premise. | |  Few ,  not many ,  not often  | A small number or low frequency in context. No exact numerical boundary follows. | |  No ,  none ,  zero  | Not a single member fits. | |  Not all  | At least one member does  not  fit. |\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t665 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t666 text Few  is worth separating from  a few . “A few books are hardcover” affirms that at least some are. “Few books are hardcover” stresses how small the number is. It often suggests some in ordinary speech, but it does not set a dependable numerical minimum. “Not many” can include zero. A hundred menu items could make five feel like few; in a menu of six, five would not feel like few. Do not quietly replace any of these phrases with a fixed number.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t667 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t668 text Most  is different: it crosses a precise line,  more than half . Words such as  the majority  plainly express that idea. Can you assign each one an exact minimum and maximum? What does “not all are Belgian” guarantee?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t673 text Worked answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t674 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t675 text The first three do  not  have fixed numerical boundaries. “Many” suggests more than an isolated example, while “few” and “not many” suggest a small number relative to the context. None alone licenses a specific cutoff such as five or ten. “Not all” is exact about one thing:  at least one beer is not Belgian .\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t676 heading Pop quiz: decide whether the overlap follows, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t677 text Pop quiz: decide whether the overlap follows\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t678 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t679 text For each pair, decide whether it guarantees  some A are C . It covers reading how students are doing ("how is Celia doing", "what does Lydia have", "who is overdue", "who has gone quiet", "Celia\'s weakest question types", "Avneet\'s last sections"). It covers accounts and upkeep: new signups ("who signed up", "did anyone new join"), access ("give Venusa access", "turn on drills for X", "what can X see"), archiving, moving a due date, unassigning, booking passes ("how many sessions does Sandra have left"), notifications, and reading or marking messages ("who messaged me", "show my thread with Celia"). It is the one place for any operation on the LSAT U platform, and none of it uses Lovable.\r\n---\r\n\r\n# Assign work on LSAT U\r\n\r\nAssign work, message students, and read how they are doing on LSAT U, all\r\nfrom the command line. That\r\ncheckout is on whatever branch another session left it on, sometimes with an\r\nuncommitted `assign.ts` that is missing flags. On 2026-09-23 it had no\r\n`--section`, `--due` or `--set`. The wrapper runs writes from\r\n`projects/.lsatu-ops`, a detached worktree it fast-forwards to `origin/main`\r\nbefore every run. It refuses to run if that copy has local edits.\r\n\r\n**Writes**\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student "Celia" --activity "Read, Recall, Colour"\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student "Lydia" --drill "main-conclusion-1"\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student "Dakota" --message "Start with PT105.S2 before Thursday."\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student "Avneet" --section PT156.S2 --due 2026-09-26\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student "Avneet" --set "PT156.S2 (LR)"\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Many students at once.** The wrapper resolves every name first, and one bad\r\nname stops the batch before anyone is emailed. The 3+ confirmation rule above\r\nstill applies.\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign-many "Celia, Lydia, Dakota" --drill "main-conclusion-1" --due 2026-09-26\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Reads.** These never write, so they are safe any time and need no confirmation:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu status "Celia"            # open work, overdue flags, last seen, recent sections\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu qtypes "Celia" --days 30  # accuracy by question type, weakest first\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu sections "Celia"          # recent timed sections with BR scores\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu overdue                   # every past-due unfinished item, all students\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu quiet --days 7            # students with open work, not seen in N days\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu students                  # every account, email, last seen\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu inbox --days 7            # messages students sent you, newest first\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu thread "Celia"            # the full message thread with one student\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Accounts, access, and Classroom upkeep** (`system/scripts/lsatu-admin.mjs`, same\r\nadmin login, calls the same `admin-manage-users` / `booking-pass-admin` edge\r\nfunctions the dashboard calls):\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu signups --days 30                  # who joined, and what access each has (NO ACCESS YET = waiting on you)\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu access "Venusa"                    # show every flag, on and off\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu access "Venusa" --template standard   # trial | standard | full, exactly the dashboard templates\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu access "Venusa" --grant drill,activity --revoke chat\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu archive "Name" --reason "finished"   # and: unarchive "Name"\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu items "Celia"                      # message it to the student, then mark posted\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu uploads [--all]                     # student uploads not yet reviewed\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu upload-review <id> parsed|needs_review|failed\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu notes [--all]                       # session notes waiting on a match\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu note-resolve <ledger-id> "Celia"    # file the note under her\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu note-discard <ledger-id> [--reason ".."]\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu scan-notes                          # message ids\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu unsend <message-id> [--dry-run]\r\nsystem/scripts/lsatu unsend-last "Adriana" [--dry-run]   # your most recent message to her\r\n```\r\n\r\nThis removes only your own messages, never a student\'s. It reports whether\r\nshe has already opened the thread: if she has not, she never sees the\r\nmessage. A plain message makes no bell entry and no email, so removing it\r\nremoves every trace. An assignment\'s email cannot be recalled, and unsending\r\nits inbox message does not unassign the work; use `unassign` for that.\r\nDeleting is permanent, so confirm with Joshua every time unless he named the\r\nmessage in this turn.\r\n\r\n**Multi-line text is refused on purpose.** On Windows the npx shim cuts an\r\nargument at the first newline and drops everything after it, `--dry-run`\r\nincluded. The wrapper now refuses any multi-line argument.\r\nMessages must be one line until `assign.ts` reads its text from a file.\r\n\r\nEvery write here takes `--dry-run`. Flag short names: practice, drill,\r\nclassroom, bootcamp, analytics, schedule, waj, journal, flagged, chat, export,\r\nta, activity. Templates always leave the "paying student" defaults on, the\r\nsame as the dashboard does.\r\n\r\n**Go without asking:** every read, `access` grants for one named student,\r\n`due`, and `read`. **Confirm first:** `archive`, `unarchive`, `unassign`,\r\n`--all-off`, and any `--revoke`, because each of these takes something away\r\nfrom a real student. **Not available here on purpose:** deleting a student\r\n(permanent), changing admin roles, and anything that edits app code or the\r\ndatabase schema. Those stay with Joshua in the dashboard or Lovable.\r\n\r\n**Other platform jobs that already have a home:** one-off booking links and\r\nnew passes go through the `booking-link` skill (`scripts/booking-link.ts`).\r\nAccommodations emails use the `accommodations-email` skill.\r\n\r\nAdd `--json` to any read when you want to compute on the output. `overdue` and\r\n`quiet` include former students, because the platform has no "former" flag.\r\nCross-check `students/roster.generated.md` before acting on either list.\r\n\r\nWhen you are unsure what a student already has, run `status` before\r\nassigning. One call catches both double-assigns and the overdue pile.\r\n\r\nFlags: `--schedule YYYY-MM-DD` unlocks the work that morning. `--due YYYY-MM-DD`\r\nis due at the end of that local day and shows on the card and the calendar\r\nstrip. `--dry-run` resolves the student and the work and writes nothing — use it\r\nwhen the name is at all uncertain.\r\n\r\n**Dates are absolute.** "Due Saturday" means look up the date of the coming\r\nSaturday and pass that. On 2026-09-10 (a Thursday) Saturday was 2026-09-12; a\r\nhandoff once carried 09-13, which is the Sunday.\r\n\r\nTo pace a student over several days, run the command once per day with a\r\n`--schedule` on each. Each run is its own assignment, its own row, and its own\r\nemail, so she is told about each day rather than handed a block.\r\n\r\nEvery assignment lands on the home calendar strip and the cell opens that\r\nassignment — scheduled work on its unlock day, unscheduled work on the day you\r\nassigned it. Nothing needs to be written by hand to put work on the calendar;\r\nif an assignment is missing from the band, that is a bug to fix in\r\n`useClassroomHome`, not something to patch into `classroom_items`.\r\n\r\nAlways `--dry-run` first for a student you have not assigned to before in this\r\nsession. It costs one second and it is the only cheap way to catch a wrong\r\naccount.\r\n\r\n## Why a script and not a direct DB write\r\n\r\n`scripts/assign.ts` calls the app\'s **own** `assignWork()` from\r\n`src/lib/assignWork.ts`. Assigning touches seven tables — the assignment\r\nsnapshot, `classroom_items`, the conversation and its participants, `messages`,\r\n`notifications` — plus the email edge function, and it rolls the whole thing\r\nback if the classroom item or notify throws. There is no RPC and no edge\r\nfunction for it; it is client-side code.\r\n\r\nSo never hand-write these rows. A second implementation drifts from the UI the\r\nfirst time the app changes, and produces assignments subtly unlike the ones\r\nJoshua makes by clicking.\r\n\r\n## Credentials\r\n\r\nRead from `~/ai-os/.env`, which is **not** a git repo:\r\n\r\n- `LSATPREP_ADMIN_EMAIL`, `LSATPREP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — already set\r\n\r\nNever put a credential in `projects/lsatu/.env`. That file **is tracked in git**\r\nand would be committed. The script signs in as Joshua and works under normal\r\nadmin RLS, the same permission path the UI uses.\r\n\r\n`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is deliberately **not** used even when present: it\r\nbypasses RLS on every write, so a script running as service_role would hide an\r\nRLS regression instead of hitting it. The script warns and falls back.\r\n\r\n## Expected output\r\n\r\n```\r\nAssign "Read, Recall, Colour" → Celia <celiacutler@gmail.com>\r\nAssigned. id=e83e2193-…\r\n  inbox ok · bell ok · email ok\r\n```\r\n\r\nA notify channel reading `FAILED` is **not** an assignment failure — the work is\r\nin her Classroom and only a message went missing. Report it, do not re-run.\r\n\r\n## Failure modes\r\n\r\n**`duplicate key … activity_assignments_active_unique`** — she already holds an\r\nactive assignment for this Activity. Not a bug; the DB refusing a double-assign.\r\nCheck what she has before re-trying (below).\r\n\r\n**`"X" is ambiguous`** — the script lists every matching account and stops.\r\nPick the full name or the email. Never guess: a misdirected assignment is\r\nsilent, because she simply never sees it.\r\n\r\n**Sign-in failed** — the credentials in `~/ai-os/.env` are wrong or the account\r\ngained MFA.\r\n\r\n## Checking what a student already has\r\n\r\n`system/scripts/lsatu status "Celia"` lists every open classroom item with its\r\ntype, status, assign date and due date, and flags anything overdue.\r\n\r\n## A PT section as timed homework\r\n\r\n`--section PT156.S2` (also accepts `PT156-S2`, `pt 156 s 2`) assigns one\r\nLogical Reasoning section to run under the real 35:00 section clock, with the\r\nofficial PrepTest header, exactly like a section inside a practice test.\r\n\r\nWhat the script does, verified end to end on 2026-09-10 on\r\n`joshua.fisseha01@gmail.com` (the test account):\r\n\r\n1. Reads `public/data/PT156-S2-LR.json` and builds the qids\r\n   `PT156-S2-Q1 … Q25` in order. No file → it lists the sections that PT does\r\n   have and stops. Only LR sections are loaded; there is no RC/LG file set.\r\n2. Finds or creates the homework set titled **`PT156.S2 (LR)`** with exactly\r\n   those qids and `estimated_minutes = 35`. One set per section, reused; a\r\n'}]

[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Wall time: 3.7848 seconds\nOutput:'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Browser tab: 1116362012, Title: "Some, Most, and All | LSAT U visual study", URL: "http://127.0.0.1:8081/quantity-statements/index.html".\n0 AXWebArea Some, Most, and All | LSAT U visual study, URL: 127.0.0.1:8081/quantity-statements/index.html\n\t1 container\n\t\t2 text September 29, 2026 | Note\n\t\t3 heading Some, Most, and All, Value: 1\n\t\t\t4 text Some, Most, and All\n\t\t5 container\n\t\t\t6 text Quantity statements tell us whether a claim applies to some members of a group, most of them, or all of them. Suppose a class has been assigned a case to read. These are three different claims about that same class:\n\t\t\t7 container Three claims about the same class\n\t\t\t\t8 text Some\n\t\t\t\t9 text students read it.\n\t\t\t\t10 text Most\n\t\t\t\t11 text students read it.\n\t\t\t\t12 text All\n\t\t\t\t13 text students read it.\n\t\t\t14 text We do not need an exact headcount to understand the difference. What must be true? What could still be true? The answer changes with the word we use.\n\t\t\t15 container Explore quantity statements with eight books\n\t\t\t\t16 text A LITTLE EXPERIMENT\n\t\t\t\t17 container\n\t\t\t\t\t18 text 1\n\t\t\t\t\t19 text  of 8 books are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t20 text Move the count. Watch which statements become true.\n\t\t\t\t21 slider (settable, integer) Description: Number of hardcover books, Value: 1, ID: quantity-slider\n\t\t\t\t22 container\n\t\t\t\t\t23 text Some 1–8 Most 5–8 All 8\n\t\t24 container Jump through the lesson\n\t\t\t25 link Description: Some, Value: 127.0.0.1:8081/quantity-statements/index.html#some\n\t\t\t26 link Description: Most, Value: 127.0.0.1:8081/quantity-statements/index.html#most\n\t\t\t27 link Description: All, Value: 127.0.0.1:8081/quantity-statements/index.html#all\n\t\t\t28 link Description: Inferences, Value: 127.0.0.1:8081/quantity-statements/index.html#inferences\n\t\t\t29 link Description: Practice, Value: 127.0.0.1:8081/quantity-statements/index.html#quantity-quiz\n\t\t\t30 link Description: Drill, Value: 127.0.0.1:8081/quantity-statements/index.html#drill\n\t\t31 heading 01 Some guarantees at least one, Value: 2, ID: some\n\t\t\t32 text 01 Some guarantees at least one\n\t\t33 container\n\t\t\t34 text Imagine a shelf with eight books. I tell you that  some of the books are hardcover . How many hardcover books must there be?\n\t\t35 container\n\t\t\t36 text At least  one . There could be one, four, or all eight. “Some” rules out zero. It does not rule out “most” or “all.”\n\t\t37 image Eight books showing that one hardcover book and eight hardcover books both satisfy some.\n\t\t38 text This is easy to miss because in ordinary conversation “some” often suggests “some, but not all.” On the LSAT, that extra phrase is not part of the statement. If all eight books are hardcover, it is still true that some are hardcover.\n\t\t39 container\n\t\t\t40 text TRY IT 01 “Some applicants received an interview.” Could every applicant have received one? Does the sentence tell us that anyone was denied an interview?\n\t\t\t41 text Your answer\n\t\t\t42 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-0\n\t\t\t43 button Check my answer \n\t\t44 container\n\t\t\t45 text Whenever you read  some , replace it with  at least one  in your head. That tells you exactly what the sentence guarantees:\n\t\t46 container\n\t\t\t47 text Some of the books are hardcover.\n\t\t\t48 text At least one of the books is hardcover.\n\t\t49 text Now focus on that one book. It belongs to both groups: it is a book, and it is hardcover. If we describe the same object from the hardcover side, we can say:\n\t\t50 container\n\t\t\t51 text Some hardcover items are books.\n\t\t\t52 text At least one hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t53 container\n\t\t\t54 text We have not found a new object. We have described the same overlap in the other direction. That is why a  some  statement works both ways:\n\t\t55 text Books  ←some→  Hardcover\n\n\t\t56 text The double arrow tells us that at least one thing belongs to both groups. It does not tell us that every book is hardcover or that every hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t57 heading What would make “some” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t58 text What would make “some” false?\n\t\t59 container\n\t\t\t60 text If  some books are hardcover  is false, then  no books are hardcover . There is not even one book in both groups. Notice the difference between  no books are hardcover  and  some books are not hardcover . The second sentence still allows other books to be hardcover, so it does not negate “some.”\n\t\t61 heading 02 Most guarantees more than half, Value: 2, ID: most\n\t\t\t62 text 02 Most guarantees more than half\n\t\t63 container\n\t\t\t64 text Now I tell you that  most of the eight books are hardcover . We need at least  five  hardcover books. Four would be exactly half, and half is not most. Five, six, seven, or eight could satisfy the sentence.\n\t\t65 image Eight books showing that five hardcover books and eight hardcover books both satisfy most.\n\t\t66 text Notice that all eight could still be hardcover. “Most” does not tell us that an exception exists.\n\t\t67 container\n\t\t\t68 text TRY IT 02 If most of the eight books are hardcover, must some of them be hardcover? Must any be paperback?\n\t\t\t69 text Your answer\n\t\t\t70 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-1\n\t\t\t71 button Check my answer \n\t\t72 container\n\t\t\t73 text Here is where the direction of the statement matters. From “most books are hardcover,” we know that  some hardcover things are books . We cannot say that  most hardcover things are books . Five of our eight shelf books could be hardcover, while a library holds hundreds of other hardcover items. The first statement counts the eight books; the reversed statement counts a different group.\n\t\t74 text Books  ─most→  Hardcover\nHardcover  ←some→  Books\n\n\t\t75 container\n\t\t\t76 text The first arrow gives the majority claim. The second line is the overlap that the majority guarantees. When we read a most statement backward, the word becomes  some .\n\t\t77 container\n\t\t\t78 text QUICK CHECK 03 A program has 100 applicants. Most speak Spanish. What is the smallest possible number who speak Spanish? What is the largest?\n\t\t\t79 text Your answer\n\t\t\t80 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-2\n\t\t\t81 button Check my answer \n\t\t82 heading What would make “most” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t83 text What would make “most” false?\n\t\t84 container\n\t\t\t85 text “Most of the eight books are hardcover” needs at least five hardcover books. Its negation permits  four or fewer . Four is exactly half, so it already makes “most” false. The opposite of “most are hardcover” is  half or fewer are hardcover , not “most are paperback.” Both kinds could make up exactly half.\n\t\t86 heading 03 All leaves no exception, Value: 2, ID: all\n\t\t\t87 text 03 All leaves no exception\n\t\t88 container\n\t\t\t89 text If  all eight books are hardcover , every book on the shelf is hardcover. One paperback on that shelf would make the statement false.\n\t\t90 image Eight books showing that all eight must be hardcover to satisfy all.\n\t\t91 container\n\t\t\t92 text An all statement gives us a rule:  if it is one of these eight books, then it is hardcover .\n\t\t93 text One of these books  →  Hardcover\nNot hardcover       →  Not one of these books\n\n\t\t94 text The second line is the contrapositive. Both lines go with the same rule. We cannot turn the first line around and conclude that every hardcover thing is a book on this shelf.\n\t\t95 container\n\t\t\t96 text TRY IT 04 You pick up a paperback. What does the rule tell you? What if you pick up a hardcover book from another shelf?\n\t\t\t97 text Your answer\n\t\t\t98 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-3\n\t\t\t99 button Check my answer \n\t\t100 text There is a small qualification. “All A are B” gives a rule about A. By itself, it does not tell us that any A exist. When we already know the group exists, all also guarantees most and some.\n\t\t101 heading What would make “all” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t102 text What would make “all” false?\n\t\t103 container\n\t\t\t104 text One exception is enough. “Not all eight books are hardcover” means  at least one of the eight is not hardcover . The other seven could still be hardcover. This is the negation of the all claim. By contrast, “not hardcover → not one of these eight books” is its  contrapositive : another way to state the original rule, not a way to deny it.\n\t\t105 heading 04 Put the three statements side by side, Value: 2\n\t\t\t106 text 04 Put the three statements side by side\n\t\t107 text The same shelf can help us see the whole range.\n\t\t108 image For eight existing books: some permits one through eight hardcover, most permits five through eight, and all requires eight.\n\t\t109 text Read the implications in one direction:\n\t\t110 text ALL  →  MOST  →  SOME       (when the group exists)\n\n\t\t111 container\n\t\t\t112 text If all eight books are hardcover, then most are, and some are. If only “some” is given, all eight  could  be hardcover, but we cannot conclude that they  are . Keep the distinction between a possible situation and a required one.\n\t\t113 heading 05 Carry a claim through an all rule, Value: 2, ID: inferences\n\t\t\t114 text 05 Carry a claim through an all rule\n\t\t115 container\n\t\t\t116 text Now we can combine statements. Suppose  some library books are mysteries  and  all mysteries are fiction . We have at least one book that is a mystery. The all rule applies to every mystery, including that one. So  some library books are fiction .\n\t\t117 text Library books  ←some→  Mysteries  →  Fiction\nLibrary books  ←some→  Fiction\n\n\t\t118 container\n\t\t\t119 text The all arrow points  away from  the mystery group we reached. That is why the chain works. If the second sentence said only “most mysteries are fiction,” the mystery books we found could be among the exceptions.\n\t\t120 image A marked library book is inside the mysteries group, which is entirely inside the fiction group.\n\t\t121 container\n\t\t\t122 text QUICK CHECK 05 Some archive documents are letters. All letters are handwritten. What follows?\n\t\t\t123 text Your answer\n\t\t\t124 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-4\n\t\t\t125 button Check my answer \n\t\t126 text The same reasoning preserves the first quantity word:\n\t\t127 table\n\t\t\t128 row\n\t\t\t\t129 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t130 text First statement\n\t\t\t\t131 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t132 text Rule\n\t\t\t\t133 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t134 text What follows\n\t\t\t135 row\n\t\t\t\t136 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t137 text Some library books are mysteries.\n\t\t\t\t138 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t139 text All mysteries are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t140 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t141 text Some library books are fiction.\n\t\t\t142 row\n\t\t\t\t143 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t144 text Most library books are mysteries.\n\t\t\t\t145 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t146 text All mysteries are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t147 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t148 text Most library books are fiction.\n\t\t\t149 row\n\t\t\t\t150 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t151 text All library books are mysteries.\n\t\t\t\t152 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t153 text All mysteries are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t154 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t155 text All library books are fiction.\n\t\t156 container\n\t\t\t157 text TRY IT 06 “Most library books are mysteries. All fiction is mystery.” Can we conclude that most library books are fiction?\n\t\t\t158 text Your answer\n\t\t\t159 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-5\n\t\t\t160 button Check my answer \n\t\t161 heading 06 Two majorities of the same group must meet, Value: 2\n\t\t\t162 text 06 Two majorities of the same group must meet\n\t\t163 container\n\t\t\t164 text Suppose a club has ten members.  Most members study law , and  most members work part time . Each “most” needs at least six of the ten members. Those two sets cannot fit inside the club without sharing at least two people.\n\t\t165 container Explore why two majorities overlap\n\t\t\t166 heading Try to separate the majorities., Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t167 text Try to separate the majorities.\n\t\t\t168 text Six of ten club members study law. Six work part time. Rearrange the workers and watch what cannot change.\n\t\t\t169 container Description: Ten club members, ID: quantity-overlap-people\n\t\t\t\t170 container Member 1: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t171 container Member 2: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t172 container Member 3: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t173 container Member 4: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t174 container Member 5: studies law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t175 container Member 6: studies law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t176 container Member 7: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t177 container Member 8: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t178 container Member 9: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t179 container Member 10: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t180 text Studies law Works part time Both\n\t\t\t181 container\n\t\t\t\t182 text 2\n\t\t\t\t183 text  members have both traits. \n\t\t\t\t184 text Even the smallest possible overlap is not zero.\n\t\t\t185 button Rearrange the workers , ID: quantity-overlap-shuffle\n\t\t\t186 container\n\t\t\t\t187 text The universe is the ten club members.  The shared middle cannot be empty.\n\t\t\t188 container Venn diagram of ten club members, updated as the members are rearranged\n\t\t\t189 text The circle areas are schematic. The numbers count members and change when you rearrange them.\n\t\t190 container\n\t\t\t191 text What is given?  More than half of the  same ten members  study law. More than half of those same ten work part time. The claims count club members, not all law students or all part-time workers everywhere.\n\t\t192 container\n\t\t\t193 text Why must they meet?  Each group needs at least six members. If the groups were separate, we would need twelve different club members. There are only ten. At least two members must be in both groups.\n\t\t194 container\n\t\t\t195 text What follows? Some law students work part time.  We can reverse that some claim:  some part-time workers study law . Both sentences describe the same overlapping members. We know at least one exists; we do not know that most law students or most part-time workers have the other trait.\n\t\t196 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             Most club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         Both majorities count the same club members.\n\n\t\t197 container\n\t\t\t198 text QUICK CHECK 07 A club has 25 members. Most are lawyers, and most play an instrument. What is the smallest possible number who are both lawyers and play an instrument?\n\t\t\t199 text Your answer\n\t\t\t200 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-6\n\t\t\t201 button Check my answer \n\t\t202 container\n\t\t\t203 text TRY IT 08 If most club members study law and most club members work part time, could the two groups of members be completely separate?\n\t\t\t204 text Your answer\n\t\t\t205 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-7\n\t\t\t206 button Check my answer \n\t\t207 heading When all describes that same group, Value: 3\n\t\t\t208 text When all describes that same group\n\t\t209 container\n\t\t\t210 text There is another way to guarantee an overlap. Suppose  most club members study law , and  all club members work part time . We already know there are law students in the club. The all rule tells us that  each one of those members  also works part time. So  some law students work part time .\n\t\t211 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             All club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         The law students already found are club members,\n             so the all rule applies to each of them.\n\n\t\t212 container\n\t\t\t213 text We can make the same move with  some . If  some club members study law  and  all club members work part time , take the member guaranteed by “some.” That person has both traits. Again,  some law students work part time . The sentences can be stated in the other order:  all club members work part time; some club members study law . The same person still proves the overlap.\n\t\t214 image An all rule covers every club member. A highlighted law student is therefore also a part-time worker.\n\t\t215 container\n\t\t\t216 text TRY IT 09 All A are B. All A are C. Must some B be C?\n\t\t\t217 text Your answer\n\t\t\t218 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-8\n\t\t\t219 button Check my answer \n\t\t220 heading 07 Two majorities can also compare group sizes, Value: 2\n\t\t\t221 text 07 Two majorities can also compare group sizes\n\t\t222 container\n\t\t\t223 text Here is a different comparison.  Most debate team members are seniors , but  most seniors are not on the debate team . The seniors on the team are more than half of the team and less than half of the seniors. The same overlap takes up a larger share of the team than of the senior class. Therefore,  there are more seniors than debate team members .\n\t\t224 image An example in which six of ten debate team members are seniors, while six of twenty seniors are on the team.\n\t\t225 text The numbers in the picture are one possible case. The conclusion follows from the two majority claims, not from those particular numbers.\n\t\t226 heading 08 Similar chains can leave a gap, Value: 2\n\t\t\t227 text 08 Similar chains can leave a gap\n\t\t228 text Two some statements need not describe the same person or thing:\n\t\t229 text Some volunteers speak Spanish.\nSome Spanish speakers are trained.\n\n\t\t230 text The trained Spanish speakers could all be people who do not volunteer. We cannot conclude that any volunteers are trained.\n\t\t231 image Two different Spanish speakers satisfy the two some claims without any volunteer being trained.\n\t\t232 text Replacing the second “some” with “most” does not fix the gap. The Spanish-speaking volunteers could sit in the untrained minority. Even two most statements that count different groups do not automatically produce a new majority claim.\n\t\t233 container\n\t\t\t234 text Before drawing a conclusion, ask:  Am I carrying a known group through an all rule? Or do two majorities count the same group?  If neither is true, check whether the groups could miss each other.\n\t\t235 container\n\t\t\t236 text QUICK CHECK 10 A club has 13 members. Most are women, and some are dancers. How many female dancers are guaranteed? They guarantee \n\t\t\t287 text some B are C\n\t\t\t288 text  only when we also know that at least one A exists. Use the sentence behind each arrow to check what it guarantees.\n\t\t289 container\n\t\t\t290 heading 10 Nearby words need a closer look, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t291 text 10 Nearby words need a closer look\n\t\t\t292 text The words around a quantity statement can look familiar without making the same promise. All may fit too.\n\t\t\t\t310 row\n\t\t\t\t\t311 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t312 text A few\n\t\t\t\t\t\t313 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t314 text several\n\t\t\t\t\t\t315 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t316 text many\n\t\t\t\t\t317 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t318 text A positive number in ordinary use, but no universal cutoff. They imply at least one.\n\t\t\t\t319 row\n\t\t\t\t\t320 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t321 text Most\n\t\t\t\t\t\t322 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t323 text more than half\n\t\t\t\t\t\t324 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t325 text a majority of\n\t\t\t\t\t326 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t327 text Strictly more than half of the named group fit.\n\t\t\t\t328 row\n\t\t\t\t\t329 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t330 text All\n\t\t\t\t\t\t331 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t332 text every\n\t\t\t\t\t\t333 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t334 text each\n\t\t\t\t\t\t335 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t336 text without exception\n\t\t\t\t\t337 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t338 text Every member of the named group fits.
