No exact numerical boundary follows.\n\t\t\t\t348 row\n\t\t\t\t\t349 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t350 text No\n\t\t\t\t\t\t351 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t352 text none\n\t\t\t\t\t\t353 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t354 text zero\n\t\t\t\t\t355 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t356 text Not a single member fits.\n\t\t\t\t357 row\n\t\t\t\t\t358 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t359 text Not all\n\t\t\t\t\t360 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t361 text At least one member does \n\t\t\t\t\t\t362 text not\n\t\t\t\t\t\t363 text  fit.\n\t\t\t364 text Few\n\t\t\t365 text  is worth separating from \n\t\t\t366 text a few\n\t\t\t367 text . “A few books are hardcover” affirms that at least some are. “Few books are hardcover” stresses how small the number is. It often suggests some in ordinary speech, but it does not set a dependable numerical minimum. “Not many” can include zero. A hundred menu items could make five feel like few; in a menu of six, five would not feel like few. Do not quietly replace any of these phrases with a fixed number.\n\t\t\t368 text Most\n\t\t\t369 text  is different: it crosses a precise line, \n\t\t\t370 text more than half\n\t\t\t371 text . [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Wall time: 8.1350 seconds\nOutput:'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Browser tab: 1116362015, Title: "Some, Most, and All | LSAT U visual study", URL: "http://127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/10-quantity-statements-student.html".\n0 AXWebArea Some, Most, and All | LSAT U visual study, URL: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/10-quantity-statements-student.html\n\t1 container\n\t\t2 text September 29, 2026 | Note\n\t\t3 heading Some, Most, and All, Value: 1\n\t\t\t4 text Some, Most, and All\n\t\t5 container\n\t\t\t6 text Quantity statements tell us whether a claim applies to some members of a group, most of them, or all of them. Suppose a class has been assigned a case to read. These are three different claims about that same class:\n\t\t\t7 container Three claims about the same class\n\t\t\t\t8 text Some\n\t\t\t\t9 text students read it.\n\t\t\t\t10 text Most\n\t\t\t\t11 text students read it.\n\t\t\t\t12 text All\n\t\t\t\t13 text students read it.\n\t\t\t14 text We do not need an exact headcount to understand the difference. What must be true? What could still be true? The answer changes with the word we use.\n\t\t\t15 container Explore quantity statements with eight books\n\t\t\t\t16 text A LITTLE EXPERIMENT\n\t\t\t\t17 container\n\t\t\t\t\t18 text 1\n\t\t\t\t\t19 text  of 8 books are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t20 text Move the count. Watch which statements become true.\n\t\t\t\t21 slider (settable, integer) Description: Number of hardcover books, Value: 1, ID: quantity-slider\n\t\t\t\t22 container\n\t\t\t\t\t23 text Some 1–8 Most 5–8 All 8\n\t\t24 container Jump through the lesson\n\t\t\t25 link Description: Some, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/10-quantity-statements-student.html#some\n\t\t\t26 link Description: Most, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/10-quantity-statements-student.html#most\n\t\t\t27 link Description: All, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/10-quantity-statements-student.html#all\n\t\t\t28 link Description: Inferences, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/10-quantity-statements-student.html#inferences\n\t\t\t29 link Description: Practice, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/10-quantity-statements-student.html#quantity-quiz\n\t\t\t30 link Description: Drill, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/10-quantity-statements-student.html#drill\n\t\t31 heading 01 Some guarantees at least one, Value: 2, ID: some\n\t\t\t32 text 01 Some guarantees at least one\n\t\t33 container\n\t\t\t34 text Imagine a shelf with eight books. I tell you that  some of the books are hardcover . How many hardcover books must there be?\n\t\t35 container\n\t\t\t36 text At least  one . There could be one, four, or all eight. “Some” rules out zero. It does not rule out “most” or “all.”\n\t\t37 image Eight books showing that one hardcover book and eight hardcover books both satisfy some.\n\t\t38 text This is easy to miss because in ordinary conversation “some” often suggests “some, but not all.” On the LSAT, that extra phrase is not part of the statement. If all eight books are hardcover, it is still true that some are hardcover.\n\t\t39 container\n\t\t\t40 text TRY IT 01 “Some applicants received an interview.” Could every applicant have received one? Does the sentence tell us that anyone was denied an interview?\n\t\t\t41 text Your answer\n\t\t\t42 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-0\n\t\t\t43 button Check my answer \n\t\t44 container\n\t\t\t45 text Whenever you read  some , replace it with  at least one  in your head. That tells you exactly what the sentence guarantees:\n\t\t46 container\n\t\t\t47 text Some of the books are hardcover.\n\t\t\t48 text At least one of the books is hardcover.\n\t\t49 text Now focus on that one book. It belongs to both groups: it is a book, and it is hardcover. If we describe the same object from the hardcover side, we can say:\n\t\t50 container\n\t\t\t51 text Some hardcover items are books.\n\t\t\t52 text At least one hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t53 container\n\t\t\t54 text We have not found a new object. We have described the same overlap in the other direction. That is why a  some  statement works both ways:\n\t\t55 text Books  ←some→  Hardcover\n\n\t\t56 text The double arrow tells us that at least one thing belongs to both groups. It does not tell us that every book is hardcover or that every hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t57 heading What would make “some” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t58 text What would make “some” false?\n\t\t59 container\n\t\t\t60 text If  some books are hardcover  is false, then  no books are hardcover . There is not even one book in both groups. Notice the difference between  no books are hardcover  and  some books are not hardcover . The second sentence still allows other books to be hardcover, so it does not negate “some.”\n\t\t61 heading 02 Most guarantees more than half, Value: 2, ID: most\n\t\t\t62 text 02 Most guarantees more than half\n\t\t63 container\n\t\t\t64 text Now I tell you that  most of the eight books are hardcover . We need at least  five  hardcover books. Four would be exactly half, and half is not most. Five, six, seven, or eight could satisfy the sentence.\n\t\t65 image Eight books showing that five hardcover books and eight hardcover books both satisfy most.\n\t\t66 text Notice that all eight could still be hardcover. “Most” does not tell us that an exception exists.\n\t\t67 container\n\t\t\t68 text TRY IT 02 If most of the eight books are hardcover, must some of them be hardcover? Must any be paperback?\n\t\t\t69 text Your answer\n\t\t\t70 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-1\n\t\t\t71 button Check my answer \n\t\t72 container\n\t\t\t73 text Here is where the direction of the statement matters. From “most books are hardcover,” we know that  some hardcover things are books . We cannot say that  most hardcover things are books . Five of our eight shelf books could be hardcover, while a library holds hundreds of other hardcover items. The first statement counts the eight books; the reversed statement counts a different group.\n\t\t74 text Books  ─most→  Hardcover\nHardcover  ←some→  Books\n\n\t\t75 container\n\t\t\t76 text The first arrow gives the majority claim. The second line is the overlap that the majority guarantees. When we read a most statement backward, the word becomes  some .\n\t\t77 container\n\t\t\t78 text QUICK CHECK 03 A program has 100 applicants. Most speak Spanish. What is the smallest possible number who speak Spanish? What is the largest?\n\t\t\t79 text Your answer\n\t\t\t80 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-2\n\t\t\t81 button Check my answer \n\t\t82 heading What would make “most” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t83 text What would make “most” false?\n\t\t84 container\n\t\t\t85 text “Most of the eight books are hardcover” needs at least five hardcover books. Its negation permits  four or fewer . Four is exactly half, so it already makes “most” false. The opposite of “most are hardcover” is  half or fewer are hardcover , not “most are paperback.” Both kinds could make up exactly half.\n\t\t86 heading 03 All leaves no exception, Value: 2, ID: all\n\t\t\t87 text 03 All leaves no exception\n\t\t88 container\n\t\t\t89 text If  all eight books are hardcover , every book on the shelf is hardcover. One paperback on that shelf would make the statement false.\n\t\t90 image Eight books showing that all eight must be hardcover to satisfy all.\n\t\t91 container\n\t\t\t92 text An all statement gives us a rule:  if it is one of these eight books, then it is hardcover .\n\t\t93 text One of these books  →  Hardcover\nNot hardcover       →  Not one of these books\n\n\t\t94 text The second line is the contrapositive. Both lines go with the same rule. We cannot turn the first line around and conclude that every hardcover thing is a book on this shelf.\n\t\t95 container\n\t\t\t96 text TRY IT 04 You pick up a paperback. What does the rule tell you? What if you pick up a hardcover book from another shelf?\n\t\t\t97 text Your answer\n\t\t\t98 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-3\n\t\t\t99 button Check my answer \n\t\t100 text There is a small qualification. “All A are B” gives a rule about A. By itself, it does not tell us that any A exist. When we already know the group exists, all also guarantees most and some.\n\t\t101 heading What would make “all” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t102 text What would make “all” false?\n\t\t103 container\n\t\t\t104 text One exception is enough. “Not all eight books are hardcover” means  at least one of the eight is not hardcover . The other seven could still be hardcover. This is the negation of the all claim. By contrast, “not hardcover → not one of these eight books” is its  contrapositive : another way to state the original rule, not a way to deny it.\n\t\t105 heading 04 Put the three statements side by side, Value: 2\n\t\t\t106 text 04 Put the three statements side by side\n\t\t107 text The same shelf can help us see the whole range.\n\t\t108 image For eight existing books: some permits one through eight hardcover, most permits five through eight, and all requires eight.\n\t\t109 text Read the implications in one direction:\n\t\t110 text ALL  →  MOST  →  SOME       (when the group exists)\n\n\t\t111 container\n\t\t\t112 text If all eight books are hardcover, then most are, and some are. If only “some” is given, all eight  could  be hardcover, but we cannot conclude that they  are . Keep the distinction between a possible situation and a required one.\n\t\t113 heading 05 Carry a claim through an all rule, Value: 2, ID: inferences\n\t\t\t114 text 05 Carry a claim through an all rule\n\t\t115 container\n\t\t\t116 text Now we can combine statements. Suppose  some library books are mysteries  and  all mysteries are fiction . We have at least one book that is a mystery. The all rule applies to every mystery, including that one. So  some library books are fiction .\n\t\t117 text Library books  ←some→  Mysteries  →  Fiction\nLibrary books  ←some→  Fiction\n\n\t\t118 container\n\t\t\t119 text The all arrow points  away from  the mystery group we reached. That is why the chain works. If the second sentence said only “most mysteries are fiction,” the mystery books we found could be among the exceptions.\n\t\t120 image A marked library book is inside the mysteries group, which is entirely inside the fiction group.\n\t\t121 container\n\t\t\t122 text QUICK CHECK 05 Some archive documents are letters. All letters are handwritten. What follows?\n\t\t\t123 text Your answer\n\t\t\t124 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-4\n\t\t\t125 button Check my answer \n\t\t126 text The same reasoning preserves the first quantity word:\n\t\t127 table\n\t\t\t128 row\n\t\t\t\t129 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t130 text First statement\n\t\t\t\t131 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t132 text Rule\n\t\t\t\t133 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t134 text What follows\n\t\t\t135 row\n\t\t\t\t136 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t137 text Some library books are mysteries.\n\t\t\t\t138 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t139 text All mysteries are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t140 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t141 text Some library books are fiction.\n\t\t\t142 row\n\t\t\t\t143 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t144 text Most library books are mysteries.\n\t\t\t\t145 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t146 text All mysteries are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t147 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t148 text Most library books are fiction.\n\t\t\t149 row\n\t\t\t\t150 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t151 text All library books are mysteries.\n\t\t\t\t152 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t153 text All mysteries are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t154 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t155 text All library books are fiction.\n\t\t156 container\n\t\t\t157 text TRY IT 06 “Most library books are mysteries. All fiction is mystery.” Can we conclude that most library books are fiction?\n\t\t\t158 text Your answer\n\t\t\t159 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-5\n\t\t\t160 button Check my answer \n\t\t161 heading 06 Two majorities of the same group must meet, Value: 2\n\t\t\t162 text 06 Two majorities of the same group must meet\n\t\t163 container\n\t\t\t164 text Suppose a club has ten members.  Most members study law , and  most members work part time . Each “most” needs at least six of the ten members. Those two sets cannot fit inside the club without sharing at least two people.\n\t\t165 container Explore why two majorities overlap\n\t\t\t166 heading Try to separate the majorities., Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t167 text Try to separate the majorities.\n\t\t\t168 text Six of ten club members study law. Six work part time. Rearrange the workers and watch what cannot change.\n\t\t\t169 container Description: Ten club members, ID: quantity-overlap-people\n\t\t\t\t170 container Member 1: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t171 container Member 2: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t172 container Member 3: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t173 container Member 4: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t174 container Member 5: studies law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t175 container Member 6: studies law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t176 container Member 7: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t177 container Member 8: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t178 container Member 9: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t179 container Member 10: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t180 text Studies law Works part time Both\n\t\t\t181 container\n\t\t\t\t182 text 2\n\t\t\t\t183 text  members have both traits. \n\t\t\t\t184 text Even the smallest possible overlap is not zero.\n\t\t\t185 button Rearrange the workers , ID: quantity-overlap-shuffle\n\t\t\t186 container\n\t\t\t\t187 text The universe is the ten club members.  The shared middle cannot be empty.\n\t\t\t188 container Venn diagram of ten club members, updated as the members are rearranged\n\t\t\t189 text The circle areas are schematic. The numbers count members and change when you rearrange them.\n\t\t190 container\n\t\t\t191 text What is given?  More than half of the  same ten members  study law. More than half of those same ten work part time. The claims count club members, not all law students or all part-time workers everywhere.\n\t\t192 container\n\t\t\t193 text Why must they meet?  Each group needs at least six members. If the groups were separate, we would need twelve different club members. There are only ten. At least two members must be in both groups.\n\t\t194 container\n\t\t\t195 text What follows? Some law students work part time.  We can reverse that some claim:  some part-time workers study law . Both sentences describe the same overlapping members. We know at least one exists; we do not know that most law students or most part-time workers have the other trait.\n\t\t196 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             Most club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         Both majorities count the same club members.\n\n\t\t197 container\n\t\t\t198 text QUICK CHECK 07 A club has 25 members. Most are lawyers, and most play an instrument. What is the smallest possible number who are both lawyers and play an instrument?\n\t\t\t199 text Your answer\n\t\t\t200 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-6\n\t\t\t201 button Check my answer \n\t\t202 container\n\t\t\t203 text TRY IT 08 If most club members study law and most club members work part time, could the two groups of members be completely separate?\n\t\t\t204 text Your answer\n\t\t\t205 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-7\n\t\t\t206 button Check my answer \n\t\t207 heading When all describes that same group, Value: 3\n\t\t\t208 text When all describes that same group\n\t\t209 container\n\t\t\t210 text There is another way to guarantee an overlap. Suppose  most club members study law , and  all club members work part time . We already know there are law students in the club. The all rule tells us that  each one of those members  also works part time. So  some law students work part time .\n\t\t211 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             All club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         The law students already found are club members,\n             so the all rule applies to each of them.\n\n\t\t212 container\n\t\t\t213 text We can make the same move with  some . If  some club members study law  and  all club members work part time , take the member guaranteed by “some.” That person has both traits. Again,  some law students work part time . The sentences can be stated in the other order:  all club members work part time; some club members study law . The same person still proves the overlap.\n\t\t214 image An all rule covers every club member. A highlighted law student is therefore also a part-time worker.\n\t\t215 container\n\t\t\t216 text TRY IT 09 All A are B. All A are C. Must some B be C?\n\t\t\t217 text Your answer\n\t\t\t218 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-8\n\t\t\t219 button Check my answer \n\t\t220 heading 07 Two majorities can also compare group sizes, Value: 2\n\t\t\t221 text 07 Two majorities can also compare group sizes\n\t\t222 container\n\t\t\t223 text Here is a different comparison.  Most debate team members are seniors , but  most seniors are not on the debate team . The seniors on the team are more than half of the team and less than half of the seniors. The same overlap takes up a larger share of the team than of the senior class. Therefore,  there are more seniors than debate team members .\n\t\t224 image An example in which six of ten debate team members are seniors, while six of twenty seniors are on the team.\n\t\t225 text The numbers in the picture are one possible case. The conclusion follows from the two majority claims, not from those particular numbers.\n\t\t226 heading 08 Similar chains can leave a gap, Value: 2\n\t\t\t227 text 08 Similar chains can leave a gap\n\t\t228 text Two some statements need not describe the same person or thing:\n\t\t229 text Some volunteers speak Spanish.\nSome Spanish speakers are trained.\n\n\t\t230 text The trained Spanish speakers could all be people who do not volunteer. We cannot conclude that any volunteers are trained.\n\t\t231 image Two different Spanish speakers satisfy the two some claims without any volunteer being trained.\n\t\t232 text Replacing the second “some” with “most” does not fix the gap. The Spanish-speaking volunteers could sit in the untrained minority. Even two most statements that count different groups do not automatically produce a new majority claim.\n\t\t233 container\n\t\t\t234 text Before drawing a conclusion, ask:  Am I carrying a known group through an all rule? Or do two majorities count the same group?  If neither is true, check whether the groups could miss each other.\n\t\t235 container\n\t\t\t236 text QUICK CHECK 10 A club has 13 members. Most are women, and some are dancers. How many female dancers are guaranteed? All may fit too.\n\t\t\t\t310 row\n\t\t\t\t\t311 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t312 text A few\n\t\t\t\t\t\t313 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t314 text several\n\t\t\t\t\t\t315 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t316 text many\n\t\t\t\t\t317 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t318 text A positive number in ordinary use, but no universal cutoff. They imply at least one.\n\t\t\t\t319 row\n\t\t\t\t\t320 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t321 text Most\n\t\t\t\t\t\t322 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t323 text more than half\n\t\t\t\t\t\t324 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t325 text a majority of\n\t\t\t\t\t326 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t327 text Strictly more than half of the named group fit.\n\t\t\t\t328 row\n\t\t\t\t\t329 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t330 text All\n\t\t\t\t\t\t331 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t332 text every\n\t\t\t\t\t\t333 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t334 text each\n\t\t\t\t\t\t335 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t336 text without exception\n\t\t\t\t\t337 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t338 text Every member of the named group fits. No exact numerical boundary follows.\n\t\t\t\t348 row\n\t\t\t\t\t349 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t350 text No\n\t\t\t\t\t\t351 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t352 text none\n\t\t\t\t\t\t353 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t354 text zero\n\t\t\t\t\t355 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t356 text Not a single member fits.\n\t\t\t\t357 row\n\t\t\t\t\t358 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t359 text Not all\n\t\t\t\t\t360 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t361 text At least one member does \n\t\t\t\t\t\t362 text not\n\t\t\t\t\t\t363 text  fit.\n\t\t\t364 text Few\n\t\t\t365 text  is worth separating from \n\t\t\t366 text a few\n\t\t\t367 text . “A few books are hardcover” affirms that at least some are. “Few books are hardcover” stresses how small the number is. It often suggests some in ordinary speech, but it does not set a dependable numerical minimum. “Not many” can include zero. A hundred menu items could make five feel like few; in a menu of six, five would not feel like few. Do not quietly replace any of these phrases with a fixed number.\n\t\t\t368 text Most\n\t\t\t369 text  is different: it crosses a precise line, \n\t\t\t370 text more than half\n\t\t\t371 text . For a guided walkthrough and variations (stateless servers, JSON-only responses, SSE compatibility, OAuth, etc.), see [docs/server.md](docs/server.md) and\r\n[docs/client.md](docs/client.md).\r\n\r\n## Core Concepts\r\n\r\n### Servers and transports\r\n\r\nAn MCP server is typically created with `McpServer` and connected to a transport such as Streamable HTTP or stdio. The SDK supports:\r\n\r\n- **Streamable HTTP** for remote servers (recommended).\r\n- **HTTP + SSE** for backwards compatibility only.\r\n- **stdio** for local, process-spawned integrations.\r\n\r\nRunnable server examples live under `src/examples/server` and are documented in [docs/server.md](docs/server.md).\r\n\r\n### Tools, resources, prompts\r\n\r\n- **Tools** let LLMs ask your server to take actions (computation, side effects, network calls).\r\n- **Resources** expose read-only data that clients can surface to users or models.\r\n- **Prompts** are reusable templates that help users talk to models in a consistent way.\r\n\r\nThe detailed APIs, including `ResourceTemplate`, completions, and display-name metadata, are covered in [docs/server.md](docs/server.md#tools-resources-and-prompts), with runnable implementations in [`simpleStreamableHttp.ts`](src/examples/server/simpleStreamableHttp.ts).\r\n\r\n### Capabilities: sampling, elicitation, and tasks\r\n\r\nThe SDK includes higher-level capabilities for richer workflows:\r\n\r\n- **Sampling**: server-side tools can ask connected clients to run LLM completions.\r\n- **Form elicitation**: tools can request non-sensitive input via structured forms.\r\n- **URL elicitation**: servers can ask users to complete secure flows in a browser (e.g., API key entry, payments, OAuth).\r\n- **Tasks (experimental)**: long-running tool calls can be turned into tasks that you poll or resume later.\r\n\r\nConceptual overviews and links to runnable examples are in:\r\n\r\n- [docs/capabilities.md](docs/capabilities.md)\r\n\r\nKey example servers include:\r\n\r\n- [`toolWithSampleServer.ts`](src/examples/server/toolWithSampleServer.ts)\r\n- [`elicitationFormExample.ts`](src/examples/server/elicitationFormExample.ts)\r\n- [`elicitationUrlExample.ts`](src/examples/server/elicitationUrlExample.ts)\r\n\r\n### Clients\r\n\r\nThe high-level `Client` class connects to MCP servers over different transports and exposes helpers like `listTools`, `callTool`, `listResources`, `readResource`, `listPrompts`, and `getPrompt`.\r\n\r\nRunnable clients live under `src/examples/client` and are described in [docs/client.md](docs/client.md), including:\r\n\r\n- Interactive Streamable HTTP client ([`simpleStreamableHttp.ts`](src/examples/client/simpleStreamableHttp.ts))\r\n- Streamable HTTP client with SSE fallback ([`streamableHttpWithSseFallbackClient.ts`](src/examples/client/streamableHttpWithSseFallbackClient.ts))\r\n- OAuth-enabled clients and polling/parallel examples\r\n\r\n### Node.js Web Crypto (globalThis.crypto) compatibility\r\n\r\nSome parts of the SDK (for example, JWT-based client authentication in `auth-extensions.ts` via `jose`) rely on the Web Crypto API exposed as `globalThis.crypto`.\r\n\r\nSee [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md) for details on supported Node.js versions and how to polyfill `globalThis.crypto` when running on older Node.js runtimes.\r\n\r\n## Examples\r\n\r\nThe SDK ships runnable examples under `src/examples`. Use these tables to find the scenario you care about and jump straight to the corresponding code and docs.\r\n\r\n### Server examples\r\n\r\n| Scenario                                            | Description                                                                                       | Example file(s)                                                                                          | Related docs                                                             |\r\n| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\r\n| Streamable HTTP server (stateful)                   | Feature-rich server with tools, resources, prompts, logging, tasks, sampling, and optional OAuth. | [`simpleStreamableHttp.ts`](src/examples/server/simpleStreamableHttp.ts)                                 | [`server.md`](docs/server.md), [`capabilities.md`](docs/capabilities.md) |\r\n| Streamable HTTP server (stateless)                  | No session tracking; good for simple API-style servers.                                           | [`simpleStatelessStreamableHttp.ts`](src/examples/server/simpleStatelessStreamableHttp.ts)               | [`server.md`](docs/server.md)                                            |\r\n| JSON response mode (no SSE)                         | Streamable HTTP with JSON responses only and limited notifications.                               | [`jsonResponseStreamableHttp.ts`](src/examples/server/jsonResponseStreamableHttp.ts)                     | [`server.md`](docs/server.md)                                            |\r\n| Server notifications over Streamable HTTP           | Demonstrates server-initiated notifications using SSE with Streamable HTTP.                       | [`standaloneSseWithGetStreamableHttp.ts`](src/examples/server/standaloneSseWithGetStreamableHttp.ts)     | [`server.md`](docs/server.md)                                            |\r\n'}]

## assistant

I found the key gap: LSAT U already has a headless, idempotent note posting RPC, but the student note view sanitizes away scripts. I’m changing that view to run only explicitly marked interactive lessons inside a sandboxed frame. After that one platform update, a local MCP tool can post a self-contained HTML lesson directly to one student, with no Chrome step for each assignment.

Verifies the new item and archives the prior same-title note. No browser is used.',\n+  inputSchema: {\n+    student: z.string().min(2).describe('Exact student email or unambiguous name.'),\n+    html_file: z.string().min(1).describe('Absolute path to a self-contained, marked HTML lesson inside the AI OS workspace.'),\n+    title: z.string().min(1).max(160),\n+    dry_run: z.boolean().optional(),\n+  },\n+  annotations: { readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false, idempotentHint: true },\n+}, async ({ student, html_file, title, dry_run }) => {\n+  const args = [admin, 'post-lesson', student, html_file, '--title', title];\n+  if (dry_run) args.push('--dry-run');\n+  try {\n+    const { stdout } = await run(process.execPath, args, {\n+      cwd: vault,\n+      windowsHide: true,\n+      maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024,\n+      timeout: 120000,\n+    });\n+    return { content: [{ type: 'text', text: stdout.trim() }] };\n+  } catch (error) {\n+    return { isError: true, content: [{ type: 'text', text: String(error.stderr || error.message).trim() }] };\n+  }\n+});\n+\n+server.registerTool('list_student_classroom_items', {\n+  title: 'List a student’s LSAT U Classroom items',\n+  description: 'Read the current Classroom items and IDs for one student.',\n+  inputSchema: { student: z.string().min(2) },\n+  annotations: { readOnlyHint: true },\n+}, async ({ student }) => {\n+  try {\n+    const { stdout } = await run(process.execPath, [admin, 'items', student], {\n+      cwd: vault,\n+      windowsHide: true,\n+      maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024,\n+      timeout: 120000,\n+    });\n+    return { content: [{ type: 'text', text: stdout.trim() }] };\n+  } catch (error) {\n+    return { isError: true, content: [{ type: 'text', text: String(error.stderr || error.message).trim() }] };\n+  }\n+});\n+\n+await server.connect(new StdioServerTransport());\n*** End Patch"));

Suppose a class has been assigned a case to read. These are three different claims about that same class:\n\t\t\t\t\t9 container Three claims about the same class\n\t\t\t\t\t\t10 text Some\n\t\t\t\t\t\t11 text students read it.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t12 text Most\n\t\t\t\t\t\t13 text students read it.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t14 text All\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15 text students read it.\n\t\t\t\t\t16 text We do not need an exact headcount to understand the difference. What must be true? What could still be true? The answer changes with the word we use.\n\t\t\t\t\t17 container Explore quantity statements with eight books\n\t\t\t\t\t\t18 text A LITTLE EXPERIMENT\n\t\t\t\t\t\t19 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t20 text 1\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t21 text  of 8 books are hardcover\n\t\t\t\t\t\t22 text Move the count. Watch which statements become true.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t23 slider (settable, integer) Description: Number of hardcover books, Value: 1, ID: quantity-slider\n\t\t\t\t\t\t24 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t25 text Some 1–8 Most 5–8 All 8\n\t\t\t\t26 container Jump through the lesson\n\t\t\t\t\t27 link Description: Some, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/11-quantity-statements-sandbox-check.html#some\n\t\t\t\t\t28 link Description: Most, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/11-quantity-statements-sandbox-check.html#most\n\t\t\t\t\t29 link Description: All, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/11-quantity-statements-sandbox-check.html#all\n\t\t\t\t\t30 link Description: Inferences, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/11-quantity-statements-sandbox-check.html#inferences\n\t\t\t\t\t31 link Description: Practice, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/11-quantity-statements-sandbox-check.html#quantity-quiz\n\t\t\t\t\t32 link Description: Drill, Value: 127.0.0.1:8765/brainstorms/2026-09-28-recap-format/11-quantity-statements-sandbox-check.html#drill\n\t\t\t\t33 heading 01 Some guarantees at least one, Value: 2, ID: some\n\t\t\t\t\t34 text 01 Some guarantees at least one\n\t\t\t\t35 container\n\t\t\t\t\t36 text Imagine a shelf with eight books. I tell you that  some of the books are hardcover . How many hardcover books must there be?\n\t\t\t\t37 container\n\t\t\t\t\t38 text At least  one . There could be one, four, or all eight. “Some” rules out zero. It does not rule out “most” or “all.”\n\t\t\t\t39 image Eight books showing that one hardcover book and eight hardcover books both satisfy some.\n\t\t\t\t40 text This is easy to miss because in ordinary conversation “some” often suggests “some, but not all.” On the LSAT, that extra phrase is not part of the statement. If all eight books are hardcover, it is still true that some are hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t41 container\n\t\t\t\t\t42 text TRY IT 01 “Some applicants received an interview.” Could every applicant have received one? Does the sentence tell us that anyone was denied an interview?\n\t\t\t\t\t43 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t44 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-0\n\t\t\t\t\t45 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t46 container\n\t\t\t\t\t47 text Whenever you read  some , replace it with  at least one  in your head. That tells you exactly what the sentence guarantees:\n\t\t\t\t48 container\n\t\t\t\t\t49 text Some of the books are hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t\t50 text At least one of the books is hardcover.\n\t\t\t\t51 text Now focus on that one book. It belongs to both groups: it is a book, and it is hardcover. If we describe the same object from the hardcover side, we can say:\n\t\t\t\t52 container\n\t\t\t\t\t53 text Some hardcover items are books.\n\t\t\t\t\t54 text At least one hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t\t\t55 container\n\t\t\t\t\t56 text We have not found a new object. We have described the same overlap in the other direction. That is why a  some  statement works both ways:\n\t\t\t\t57 text Books  ←some→  Hardcover\n\n\t\t\t\t58 text The double arrow tells us that at least one thing belongs to both groups. It does not tell us that every book is hardcover or that every hardcover item is a book.\n\t\t\t\t59 heading What would make “some” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t60 text What would make “some” false?\n\t\t\t\t61 container\n\t\t\t\t\t62 text If  some books are hardcover  is false, then  no books are hardcover . There is not even one book in both groups. Notice the difference between  no books are hardcover  and  some books are not hardcover . The second sentence still allows other books to be hardcover, so it does not negate “some.”\n\t\t\t\t63 heading 02 Most guarantees more than half, Value: 2, ID: most\n\t\t\t\t\t64 text 02 Most guarantees more than half\n\t\t\t\t65 container\n\t\t\t\t\t66 text Now I tell you that  most of the eight books are hardcover . We need at least  five  hardcover books. Four would be exactly half, and half is not most. Five, six, seven, or eight could satisfy the sentence.\n\t\t\t\t67 image Eight books showing that five hardcover books and eight hardcover books both satisfy most.\n\t\t\t\t68 text Notice that all eight could still be hardcover. “Most” does not tell us that an exception exists.\n\t\t\t\t69 container\n\t\t\t\t\t70 text TRY IT 02 If most of the eight books are hardcover, must some of them be hardcover? Must any be paperback?\n\t\t\t\t\t71 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t72 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-1\n\t\t\t\t\t73 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t74 container\n\t\t\t\t\t75 text Here is where the direction of the statement matters. From “most books are hardcover,” we know that  some hardcover things are books . We cannot say that  most hardcover things are books . Five of our eight shelf books could be hardcover, while a library holds hundreds of other hardcover items. The first statement counts the eight books; the reversed statement counts a different group.\n\t\t\t\t76 text Books  ─most→  Hardcover\nHardcover  ←some→  Books\n\n\t\t\t\t77 container\n\t\t\t\t\t78 text The first arrow gives the majority claim. The second line is the overlap that the majority guarantees. When we read a most statement backward, the word becomes  some .\n\t\t\t\t79 container\n\t\t\t\t\t80 text QUICK CHECK 03 A program has 100 applicants. Most speak Spanish. What is the smallest possible number who speak Spanish? What is the largest?\n\t\t\t\t\t81 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t82 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-2\n\t\t\t\t\t83 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t84 heading What would make “most” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t85 text What would make “most” false?\n\t\t\t\t86 container\n\t\t\t\t\t87 text “Most of the eight books are hardcover” needs at least five hardcover books. Its negation permits  four or fewer . Four is exactly half, so it already makes “most” false. The opposite of “most are hardcover” is  half or fewer are hardcover , not “most are paperback.” Both kinds could make up exactly half.\n\t\t\t\t88 heading 03 All leaves no exception, Value: 2, ID: all\n\t\t\t\t\t89 text 03 All leaves no exception\n\t\t\t\t90 container\n\t\t\t\t\t91 text If  all eight books are hardcover , every book on the shelf is hardcover. One paperback on that shelf would make the statement false.\n\t\t\t\t92 image Eight books showing that all eight must be hardcover to satisfy all.\n\t\t\t\t93 container\n\t\t\t\t\t94 text An all statement gives us a rule:  if it is one of these eight books, then it is hardcover .\n\t\t\t\t95 text One of these books  →  Hardcover\nNot hardcover       →  Not one of these books\n\n\t\t\t\t96 text The second line is the contrapositive. Both lines go with the same rule. We cannot turn the first line around and conclude that every hardcover thing is a book on this shelf.\n\t\t\t\t97 container\n\t\t\t\t\t98 text TRY IT 04 You pick up a paperback. What does the rule tell you? What if you pick up a hardcover book from another shelf?\n\t\t\t\t\t99 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t100 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-3\n\t\t\t\t\t101 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t102 text There is a small qualification. “All A are B” gives a rule about A. By itself, it does not tell us that any A exist. When we already know the group exists, all also guarantees most and some.\n\t\t\t\t103 heading What would make “all” false?, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t104 text What would make “all” false?\n\t\t\t\t105 container\n\t\t\t\t\t106 text One exception is enough. “Not all eight books are hardcover” means  at least one of the eight is not hardcover . The other seven could still be hardcover. This is the negation of the all claim. By contrast, “not hardcover → not one of these eight books” is its  contrapositive : another way to state the original rule, not a way to deny it.\n\t\t\t\t107 heading 04 Put the three statements side by side, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t108 text 04 Put the three statements side by side\n\t\t\t\t109 text The same shelf can help us see the whole range.\n\t\t\t\t110 image For eight existing books: some permits one through eight hardcover, most permits five through eight, and all requires eight.\n\t\t\t\t111 text Read the implications in one direction:\n\t\t\t\t112 text ALL  →  MOST  →  SOME       (when the group exists)\n\n\t\t\t\t113 container\n\t\t\t\t\t114 text If all eight books are hardcover, then most are, and some are. If only “some” is given, all eight  could  be hardcover, but we cannot conclude that they  are . Keep the distinction between a possible situation and a required one.\n\t\t\t\t115 heading 05 Carry a claim through an all rule, Value: 2, ID: inferences\n\t\t\t\t\t116 text 05 Carry a claim through an all rule\n\t\t\t\t117 container\n\t\t\t\t\t118 text Now we can combine statements. Suppose  some library books are mysteries  and  all mysteries are fiction . We have at least one book that is a mystery. The all rule applies to every mystery, including that one. So  some library books are fiction .\n\t\t\t\t119 text Library books  ←some→  Mysteries  →  Fiction\nLibrary books  ←some→  Fiction\n\n\t\t\t\t120 container\n\t\t\t\t\t121 text The all arrow points  away from  the mystery group we reached. That is why the chain works. If the second sentence said only “most mysteries are fiction,” the mystery books we found could be among the exceptions.\n\t\t\t\t122 image A marked library book is inside the mysteries group, which is entirely inside the fiction group.\n\t\t\t\t123 container\n\t\t\t\t\t124 text QUICK CHECK 05 Some archive documents are letters. All letters are handwritten. What follows?\n\t\t\t\t\t125 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t126 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-4\n\t\t\t\t\t127 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t128 text The same reasoning preserves the first quantity word:\n\t\t\t\t129 table\n\t\t\t\t\t130 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t131 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t132 text First statement\n\t\t\t\t\t\t133 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t134 text Rule\n\t\t\t\t\t\t135 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t136 text What follows\n\t\t\t\t\t137 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t138 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t139 text Some library books are mysteries.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t140 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t141 text All mysteries are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t142 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t143 text Some library books are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t\t144 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t145 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t146 text Most library books are mysteries.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t147 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t148 text All mysteries are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t149 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t150 text Most library books are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t\t151 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t152 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t153 text All library books are mysteries.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t154 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t155 text All mysteries are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t156 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t157 text All library books are fiction.\n\t\t\t\t158 container\n\t\t\t\t\t159 text TRY IT 06 “Most library books are mysteries. All fiction is mystery.” Can we conclude that most library books are fiction?\n\t\t\t\t\t160 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t161 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-5\n\t\t\t\t\t162 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t163 heading 06 Two majorities of the same group must meet, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t164 text 06 Two majorities of the same group must meet\n\t\t\t\t165 container\n\t\t\t\t\t166 text Suppose a club has ten members.  Most members study law , and  most members work part time . Each “most” needs at least six of the ten members. Those two sets cannot fit inside the club without sharing at least two people.\n\t\t\t\t167 container Explore why two majorities overlap\n\t\t\t\t\t168 heading Try to separate the majorities., Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t\t169 text Try to separate the majorities.\n\t\t\t\t\t170 text Six of ten club members study law. Six work part time. Rearrange the workers and watch what cannot change.\n\t\t\t\t\t171 container Description: Ten club members, ID: quantity-overlap-people\n\t\t\t\t\t\t172 container Member 1: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t173 container Member 2: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t174 container Member 3: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t175 container Member 4: studies law, does not work part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t176 container Member 5: studies law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t177 container Member 6: studies law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t178 container Member 7: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t179 container Member 8: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t180 container Member 9: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t\t\t181 container Member 10: does not study law, works part time\n\t\t\t\t\t182 text Studies law Works part time Both\n\t\t\t\t\t183 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t184 text 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t185 text  members have both traits. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t186 text Even the smallest possible overlap is not zero.\n\t\t\t\t\t187 button Rearrange the workers , ID: quantity-overlap-shuffle\n\t\t\t\t\t188 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t189 text The universe is the ten club members.  The shared middle cannot be empty.\n\t\t\t\t\t190 container Venn diagram of ten club members, updated as the members are rearranged\n\t\t\t\t\t191 text The circle areas are schematic. The numbers count members and change when you rearrange them.\n\t\t\t\t192 container\n\t\t\t\t\t193 text What is given?  More than half of the  same ten members  study law. More than half of those same ten work part time. The claims count club members, not all law students or all part-time workers everywhere.\n\t\t\t\t194 container\n\t\t\t\t\t195 text Why must they meet?  Each group needs at least six members. If the groups were separate, we would need twelve different club members. There are only ten. At least two members must be in both groups.\n\t\t\t\t196 container\n\t\t\t\t\t197 text What follows? Some law students work part time.  We can reverse that some claim:  some part-time workers study law . Both sentences describe the same overlapping members. We know at least one exists; we do not know that most law students or most part-time workers have the other trait.\n\t\t\t\t198 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             Most club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         Both majorities count the same club members.\n\n\t\t\t\t199 container\n\t\t\t\t\t200 text QUICK CHECK 07 A club has 25 members. Most are lawyers, and most play an instrument. What is the smallest possible number who are both lawyers and play an instrument?\n\t\t\t\t\t201 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t202 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-6\n\t\t\t\t\t203 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t204 container\n\t\t\t\t\t205 text TRY IT 08 If most club members study law and most club members work part time, could the two groups of members be completely separate?\n\t\t\t\t\t206 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t207 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-7\n\t\t\t\t\t208 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t209 heading When all describes that same group, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t210 text When all describes that same group\n\t\t\t\t211 container\n\t\t\t\t\t212 text There is another way to guarantee an overlap. Suppose  most club members study law , and  all club members work part time . We already know there are law students in the club. The all rule tells us that  each one of those members  also works part time. So  some law students work part time .\n\t\t\t\t213 text Given:       Most club members study law.\n             All club members work part time.\nMust follow: Some law students work part time.\nWhy:         The law students already found are club members,\n             so the all rule applies to each of them.\n\n\t\t\t\t214 container\n\t\t\t\t\t215 text We can make the same move with  some . If  some club members study law  and  all club members work part time , take the member guaranteed by “some.” That person has both traits. Again,  some law students work part time . The sentences can be stated in the other order:  all club members work part time; some club members study law . The same person still proves the overlap.\n\t\t\t\t216 image An all rule covers every club member. A highlighted law student is therefore also a part-time worker.\n\t\t\t\t217 container\n\t\t\t\t\t218 text TRY IT 09 All A are B. All A are C. Must some B be C?\n\t\t\t\t\t219 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t220 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-8\n\t\t\t\t\t221 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t222 heading 07 Two majorities can also compare group sizes, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t223 text 07 Two majorities can also compare group sizes\n\t\t\t\t224 container\n\t\t\t\t\t225 text Here is a different comparison.  Most debate team members are seniors , but  most seniors are not on the debate team . The seniors on the team are more than half of the team and less than half of the seniors. The same overlap takes up a larger share of the team than of the senior class. Therefore,  there are more seniors than debate team members .\n\t\t\t\t226 image An example in which six of ten debate team members are seniors, while six of twenty seniors are on the team.\n\t\t\t\t227 text The numbers in the picture are one possible case. The conclusion follows from the two majority claims, not from those particular numbers.\n\t\t\t\t228 heading 08 Similar chains can leave a gap, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t229 text 08 Similar chains can leave a gap\n\t\t\t\t230 text Two some statements need not describe the same person or thing:\n\t\t\t\t231 text Some volunteers speak Spanish.\nSome Spanish speakers are trained.\n\n\t\t\t\t232 text The trained Spanish speakers could all be people who do not volunteer. We cannot conclude that any volunteers are trained.\n\t\t\t\t233 image Two different Spanish speakers satisfy the two some claims without any volunteer being trained.\n\t\t\t\t234 text Replacing the second “some” with “most” does not fix the gap. The Spanish-speaking volunteers could sit in the untrained minority. Even two most statements that count different groups do not automatically produce a new majority claim.\n\t\t\t\t235 container\n\t\t\t\t\t236 text Before drawing a conclusion, ask:  Am I carrying a known group through an all rule? Or do two majorities count the same group?  If neither is true, check whether the groups could miss each other.\n\t\t\t\t237 container\n\t\t\t\t\t238 text QUICK CHECK 10 A club has 13 members. Most are women, and some are dancers. How many female dancers are guaranteed? How many are possible?\n\t\t\t\t\t239 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t240 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-9\n\t\t\t\t\t241 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t242 container\n\t\t\t\t\t243 heading 09 The moves to keep, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t244 text 09 The moves to keep\n\t\t\t\t\t245 table\n\t\t\t\t\t\t246 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t247 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t248 text What you have\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t249 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t250 text What you may conclude\n\t\t\t\t\t\t251 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t252 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t253 text Some A are B\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t254 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t255 text Some B are A\n\t\t\t\t\t\t256 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t257 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t258 text Most A are B\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t259 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t260 text Some A are B, and some B are A\n\t\t\t\t\t\t261 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t262 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t263 text All A are B\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t264 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t265 text A → B, and not B → not A\n\t\t\t\t\t\t266 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t267 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t268 text Some/most/all A are B; all B are C\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t269 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t270 text The same first quantity of A are C\n\t\t\t\t\t\t271 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t272 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t273 text Most A are B; most A are C\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t274 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t275 text Some B are C\n\t\t\t\t\t\t276 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t277 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t278 text Most A are B; all A are C\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t279 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t280 text Some B are C\n\t\t\t\t\t\t281 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t282 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t283 text Some A are B; all A are C\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t284 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t285 text Some B are C\n\t\t\t\t\t286 text Two \n\t\t\t\t\t287 text all\n\t\t\t\t\t288 text  claims about A guarantee that every A has both traits. They guarantee \n\t\t\t\t\t289 text some B are C\n\t\t\t\t\t290 text  only when we also know that at least one A exists. Use the sentence behind each arrow to check what it guarantees.\n\t\t\t\t291 container\n\t\t\t\t\t292 heading 10 Nearby words need a closer look, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t293 text 10 Nearby words need a closer look\n\t\t\t\t\t294 text The words around a quantity statement can look familiar without making the same promise. Sort them by \n\t\t\t\t\t295 text what they guarantee\n\t\t\t\t\t296 text , then check the sentence in front of you:\n\t\t\t\t\t297 table\n\t\t\t\t\t\t298 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t299 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t300 text Word or phrase\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t301 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t302 text What it guarantees\n\t\t\t\t\t\t303 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t304 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t305 text Some\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t306 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t307 text at least one\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t308 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t309 text one or more\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t310 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t311 text One or more members fit. All may fit too.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t312 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t313 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t314 text A few\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t315 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t316 text several\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t317 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t318 text many\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t319 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t320 text A positive number in ordinary use, but no universal cutoff. They imply at least one.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t321 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t322 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t323 text Most\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t324 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t325 text more than half\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t326 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t327 text a majority of\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t328 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t329 text Strictly more than half of the named group fit.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t330 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t331 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t332 text All\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t333 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t334 text every\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t335 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t336 text each\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t337 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t338 text without exception\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t339 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t340 text Every member of the named group fits. The group may still need a separate existence premise.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t341 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t342 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t343 text Few\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t344 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t345 text not many\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t346 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t347 text not often\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t348 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t349 text A small number or low frequency in context. No exact numerical boundary follows.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t350 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t351 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t352 text No\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t353 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t354 text none\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t355 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t356 text zero\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t357 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t358 text Not a single member fits.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t359 row\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t360 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t361 text Not all\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t362 cell\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t363 text At least one member does \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t364 text not\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t365 text  fit.\n\t\t\t\t\t366 text Few\n\t\t\t\t\t367 text  is worth separating from \n\t\t\t\t\t368 text a few\n\t\t\t\t\t369 text . “A few books are hardcover” affirms that at least some are. “Few books are hardcover” stresses how small the number is. It often suggests some in ordinary speech, but it does not set a dependable numerical minimum. “Not many” can include zero. A hundred menu items could make five feel like few; in a menu of six, five would not feel like few. Do not quietly replace any of these phrases with a fixed number.\n\t\t\t\t\t370 text Most\n\t\t\t\t\t371 text  is different: it crosses a precise line, \n\t\t\t\t\t372 text more than half\n\t\t\t\t\t373 text . Words such as \n\t\t\t\t\t374 text the majority\n\t\t\t\t\t375 text  plainly express that idea. Words such as \n\t\t\t\t\t376 text usually\n\t\t\t\t\t377 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t378 text typically\n\t\t\t\t\t379 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t380 text generally\n\t\t\t\t\t381 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t382 text commonly\n\t\t\t\t\t383 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t384 text frequently\n\t\t\t\t\t385 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t386 text often\n\t\t\t\t\t387 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t388 text likely\n\t\t\t\t\t389 text , and \n\t\t\t\t\t390 text probably\n\t\t\t\t\t391 text  can suggest prevalence in context, but pay attention to what the sentence actually counts. “Probably” about one event, for example, is a likelihood claim, not a headcount of a group.\n\t\t\t\t\t392 text Not all\n\t\t\t\t\t393 text does\n\t\t\t\t\t394 text  give us a precise minimum: at least one exception. “Not all club members are lawyers” means \n\t\t\t\t\t395 text at least one club member is not a lawyer\n\t\t\t\t\t396 text . It does not tell us whether the other members are lawyers. QUICK CHECK 11\n\t\t\t\t\t397 text A menu lists 100 beers. “Many are Belgian,” “few are Belgian,” and “not many are Belgian” are three claims. Can you assign each one an exact minimum and maximum? What does “not all are Belgian” guarantee?\n\t\t\t\t\t398 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t399 text Your answer\n\t\t\t\t\t\t400 text entry area (settable) Your answer, ID: quantity-check-10\n\t\t\t\t\t\t401 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t402 container Can you prove the overlap?, ID: quantity-quiz\n\t\t\t\t\t403 text PRACTICE\n\t\t\t\t\t404 text 01 / 07\n\t\t\t\t\t405 heading Can you prove the overlap?, Value: 3, ID: quantity-quiz-title\n\t\t\t\t\t\t406 text Can you prove the overlap?\n\t\t\t\t\t407 text Seven short answers. Make a call, explain it, then compare your reasoning.\n\t\t\t\t\t408 container quantity-quiz-premises\n\t\t\t\t\t\t409 text GIVEN\n\t\t\t\t\t\t410 text Some A are B.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t411 text All B are C.\n\t\t\t\t\t412 container quantity-quiz-form\n\t\t\t\t\t\t413 text Must some A be C?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t414 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t415 text Start with  Yes  or  No , then tell me why.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t416 text entry area (settable) Must some A be C?, ID: quantity-quiz-input\n\t\t\t\t\t\t417 button Check my answer \n\t\t\t\t418 container\n\t\t\t\t\t419 heading 11 Short drill: diagram, combine, decide, Value: 2, ID: drill\n\t\t\t\t\t\t420 text 11 Short drill: diagram, combine, decide\n\t\t\t\t\t421 text Here are five statements about one volunteer program. \n\t\t\t\t\t422 text Volunteer\n\t\t\t\t\t423 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t424 text Spanish speaker\n\t\t\t\t\t425 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t426 text trained person\n\t\t\t\t\t427 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t428 text weekend worker\n\t\t\t\t\t429 text , and \n\t\t\t\t\t430 text student\n\t\t\t\t\t431 text  name groups of people. Treat each sentence as true.\n\t\t\t\t\t432 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t433 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t434 text 1 . Some volunteers speak Spanish.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t435 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t436 text 2 . All Spanish speakers are trained.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t437 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t438 text 3 . Most volunteers work weekends.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t439 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t440 text 4 . Most volunteers are students.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t441 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t442 text 5 . Most weekend workers are trained.\n\t\t\t\t\t443 text Diagram the five statements for yourself.
